summary: Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems, refined to declaration granularity from the reviewed integrated decomposition of Faltings' 1983 paper and its 1984 erratum. All 32 node identifiers of that decomposition are kept, with its verified locators and excerpts, and each is given what a blueprint packet needs and a decomposition does not: prerequisites resolved to the pinned libraries or to a named supplier stage, an API outline with unit tests for every definition and construction, planets, and a coverage record per layer. The reviewed library audit records all six layers as not built - neither library has a polarisation, a moduli space of abelian varieties, an arithmetic degree, a Faltings height, a p-divisible group or a Tate module of an abelian variety - so nothing here duplicates the libraries. R28.1 is Sections 2 and 3 through Satz 1; R28.2 is Section 4 through the determinant identity; R28.3 is the erratum and the corrected Satz 2; R28.4 is Section 5, Satz 3 and Satz 4 with the quaternion construction; R28.5 is Section 6 through Shafarevich finiteness and the two applications; R28.6 is the two interface statements. Four requests are filed, to the semistable reduction, Weil restriction, Weil bound and Tate module owners. Thirteen gaps are carried forward from the decomposition or added here, including two of this job's own: that Faltings' paper is paywalled and was not re-read, so the packet inherits the reviewed locators for it while the two freely available sources were re-fetched and re-hashed and both reproduce; and that five of the decomposition's supplier links point at a roadmap retired on the day of its review, which this packet re-points to the pinned library or records as needing a supplier.

nodes.title: Bemerkungen a)-d): the Hodge line ω_{A/S} of a semiabelian scheme
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme (Faltings allows an algebraic stack) and p: A → S a semiabelian scheme of relative dimension g in Faltings' sense (§2, p. 350): a smooth separated commutative group scheme whose fibres are connected of dimension g and are extensions of an abelian variety by a torus; these are the semi-abelian schemes of ShimuraCompactifications:C4. Let s: S → A be the zero section and ω_{A/S} = s^*(Ω^g_{A/S}), the Hodge line of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.2; it is a line bundle on S. Then: (a) if p is proper, ω_{A/S} ≅ p_*(Ω^g_{A/S}); (b) the formation of ω_{A/S} commutes with every base change S' → S; (c) if A = Pic^τ(C/S) for a stable curve q: C → S of genus g (for a stable curve Pic^τ = Pic^0, the fibrewise Néron–Severi groups being torsion-free), then ω_{A/S} ≅ Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/S}) with ω_{C/S} the relative dualising sheaf; (d) if S = Spec(ℂ) and p is proper, ω_{A/S} ≅ Γ(A, Ω^g_{A/ℂ}) carries the positive definite hermitian product ⟨α, β⟩ = (i/2)^g (−1)^{g(g−1)/2} ∫_A α ∧ β̄ = 2^{−g} i^{g²} ∫_A α ∧ β̄. Faltings prints (i/2)^g ∫_A α ∧ β̄, which is negative definite when g ≡ 2 or 3 mod 4 (source issue E1). The node introduces no object of its own.
hypotheses: S a scheme; the moduli applications (Lemma 2) use a Deligne–Mumford stack, reached through an étale atlas and (b)

p: A → S smooth, separated and commutative with connected fibres of dimension g, each an extension of an abelian variety by a torus; separatedness and commutativity are implicit in Faltings' 'glatte algebraische Gruppe' and explicit in the Faltings–Chai definition
for (a): p proper, i.e. A an abelian scheme

for (c): q: C → S a stable curve of genus g in the sense of Deligne–Mumford ([4]) and A = Pic^τ(C/S), which is semiabelian by Faltings' Beispiel on p. 350 (requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.4)
for (d): S = Spec(ℂ) and p proper, so that A is a complex abelian variety
proofSteps: (a), (b): for a smooth group scheme, translation identifies Ω^1_{A/S} with p^*(s^*Ω^1_{A/S}), so Ω^g_{A/S} ≅ p^*ω_{A/S}; if p is proper, p_*O_A = O_S universally (geometrically connected and reduced fibres), so p_*Ω^g_{A/S} ≅ ω_{A/S}; base change of Ω^1 and of the zero section gives (b). These are statements about R35.2's Hodge line, requested there.

(c): the Lie algebra of Pic^0(C/S) along the zero section is R^1 q_*O_C, whose dual is q_*ω_{C/S} by duality for the stable curve q; taking Λ^g gives (c). Requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.4 together with the Beispiel that Pic^τ(C/S) is semiabelian.

(d): in linear coordinates α = f dz_1 ∧ … ∧ dz_g, α ∧ ᾱ = (−1)^{g(g−1)/2} |f|² dz_1 ∧ dz̄_1 ∧ … ∧ dz_g ∧ dz̄_g and (i/2) dz_j ∧ dz̄_j = dx_j ∧ dy_j, so 2^{−g} i^{g²} ∫ α ∧ ᾱ = ∫ |f|² dV > 0; with Faltings' printed factor (i/2)^g the integral is −∫ |f|² dV for g ≡ 2, 3 mod 4 (E1). For g = 1 the two agree.
Faltings states a)–d) without proof (p. 351); the steps above are the reviewers' justification.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve over a discrete valuation ring with multiplicative reduction the semiabelian model (the identity component of the Néron model) is not proper: ω is defined through the zero section and (a) does not apply.
For A = E_1 × E_2 over ℂ and α = dz_1 ∧ dz_2, the printed (i/2)^2 ∫ α ∧ ᾱ is −vol(A) and the corrected 2^{−2} i^4 ∫ α ∧ ᾱ is +vol(A), both volumes for dx_1 dy_1 dx_2 dy_2.
For g = 1 and A = ℂ/(ℤ + τℤ), ⟨dz, dz⟩ = (i/2) ∫ dz ∧ dz̄ = Im τ.

Check (c) on two stable curves of genus 2 over a field: two elliptic curves meeting in one node (Pic^0 = E_1 × E_2, proper) and an irreducible curve with one node whose normalisation has genus 1 (Pic^0 an extension of that elliptic curve by G_m); in both cases Λ^2 of the two-dimensional space of sections of the dualising sheaf is a line.

uses.how: the modular height is the arithmetic degree of this bundle with the hermitian metric of part (d)

nodes.title: Unique extension of a homomorphism of semiabelian schemes over a dense open
nodes.statement: Let S be normal, U subset S open and dense, p_1 : A_1 -> S and p_2 : A_2 -> S semiabelian varieties and phi : A_1|U -> A_2|U a homomorphism of algebraic groups defined over U. Then phi extends uniquely to a homomorphism A_1 -> A_2 over S.
hypotheses: S normal; Faltings reduces 'sofort' to S noetherian and excellent, and in every use S is of finite type over ℤ or a Dedekind scheme
U ⊆ S open and dense
A_1, A_2 semiabelian over S (smooth, separated, commutative, fibres connected extensions of abelian varieties by tori)
φ a homomorphism of group schemes over U (not merely a morphism of schemes)

in every use in this paper (Lemma 2 over J and J̃, the Korollar over Spec(R'), §4 over Spec(R)) A_1|U and A_2|U are abelian schemes, so the discrete-valuation-ring case needed is the Néron mapping property for semiabelian models of abelian varieties
proofSteps: Uniqueness: two extensions agree on the dense open A_1|U; A_2 → S is separated, so their equaliser is closed, and A_1|U is schematically dense in A_1 (A_1 is smooth over the reduced S, hence reduced, and p_1 is open). Faltings: 'Eindeutigkeit folgt zum Beispiel durch Betrachtung von Torsionspunkten, oder auf tausend andere Arten.'

The case S = Spec of a complete discrete valuation ring is quoted as well known; for abelian generic fibres it is the Néron mapping property of the identity component of the Néron model (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud 7.4 Proposition 3), requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.1.
Reduce to S noetherian and excellent, and let X ⊆ A_1 ×_S A_2 be the closure of the graph of φ.

Base change to suitable valuation rings (the valuative criterion, Mathlib's IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion; for noetherian S discrete valuation rings whose generic point maps into U suffice) together with the discrete-valuation-ring case shows that pr_1: X → A_1 is proper with one-point fibres.

pr_1 is then proper and quasi-finite, hence finite, and birational onto the normal scheme A_1 (smooth over the normal S), so it is an isomorphism by Zariski's main theorem; X is the graph of the extension, which is a homomorphism because both sides of the homomorphism identities agree over U (uniqueness step). Neither 'proper and quasi-finite implies finite' over a non-Artinian base nor Zariski's main theorem is in the pinned libraries (Mathlib has the former only over a locally Artinian target): recorded as a gap.
acceptance: Check that the statement fails without normality of S (a cuspidal base) or without density of U.

Check on S = Spec(R), R a discrete valuation ring, with A_1 = A_2 the identity component of the Néron model of an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction, that every endomorphism of the generic fibre extends.
Check that the extension is again a group homomorphism, not merely a morphism of schemes.

Applied to the identity of the generic fibre, the lemma shows that a semiabelian model of an abelian variety over a Dedekind base is unique up to unique isomorphism; this is what makes h(A) an invariant of A_K and what the pairs of Satz 1 rely on.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 1. Sei S normal, U ⊂ S offen und dicht p_1: A_1 → S und p_2: A_2 → S zwei semiabelsche Varietäten, φ: A_1/U → A_2/U ein über U definierter Homomorphismus algebraischer Gruppen. Dann läßt sich φ eindeutig auf ganz S fortsetzen.

nodes.title: A proper stack over Spec(Z) carrying a stable curve dominating principally polarized moduli
nodes.statement: There exist over Spec(ℤ) a proper Deligne–Mumford stack J, an open substack U ⊆ J and a proper morphism ψ: U → 𝔄_g (the stack of principally polarized abelian schemes of relative dimension g, with universal abelian scheme A), extending to ψ̄: J ⊗ ℚ → Ā_g/ℚ, such that over J there are: (a) a stable curve q: C → J of some genus g̃ ≥ max(g, 2); (b) a line subbundle L ⊆ Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/J}) which is locally a direct summand (Faltings prints ω_{C/ℤ}: source issue E3); (c) over U, homomorphisms α: Pic^τ(C/J) → ψ^*(A) and β: ψ^*(A) → Pic^τ(C/J) with α ∘ β = multiplication by some d ∈ ℕ, d ≠ 0; (d) over J ⊗ ℚ an isomorphism L^{⊗r} ≅ ψ̄^*(M), where over U ⊗ ℚ the bundle L is the image of α^*: ψ^*(ω_{A/𝔄_g}) → Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/J}), and the resulting isomorphism ψ^*(ω_{A/𝔄_g})^{⊗r} ≅ ψ^*(M) over U ⊗ ℚ is the ψ^*-pullback of the isomorphism ω^{⊗r} ≅ M used to construct M on A_g. Moreover ψ̄ is surjective and ψ̄^{−1}(A_g ⊗ ℚ) ⊆ U: the Korollar uses both, the source does not state them (E4), and the J built in the proof has them. Here r, Ā_g/ℚ ⊆ ℙ^N_ℚ, Ā_g/ℤ (its closure in ℙ^N_ℤ) and M = O(1) are those fixed by Baily–Borel (fact 2 a), p. 351).
hypotheses: g ≥ 1 fixed; 𝔄_g the moduli stack over ℤ of principally polarized abelian schemes of relative dimension g with universal abelian scheme A, and A_g its coarse space (requested from PELModuli:M6)

r > 0 with (ω_{A/𝔄_g})^{⊗r} very ample on A_g/ℚ (Baily–Borel [3]); Ā_g/ℚ the closure of A_g/ℚ in ℙ^N_ℚ, Ā_g/ℤ its closure in ℙ^N_ℤ and M = O(1) on Ā_g/ℤ, extending (ω_{A/𝔄_g})^{⊗r} on Ā_g/ℚ (fact 2 a), p. 351; requested from ShimuraVarieties:V2)
M̄_g̃ the proper Deligne–Mumford stack over ℤ of stable curves of genus g̃ ≥ 2 ([4]; fact 1, p. 351): no supplier, recorded as a gap

over ℂ a proper dominant φ: N → Ā_g/ℂ over which the universal abelian scheme extends to a semiabelian scheme whose Hodge line satisfies ω^{⊗r} ≅ φ^*(M) (Namikawa [8] §9 and Faltings [6] §2; fact 2 b), pp. 351–352; requested from ShimuraCompactifications:C2 and C4)
proofSteps: At the generic point of 𝔄_g the abelian variety is a quotient α: Jac(C_η) → A_η of the Jacobian of a smooth curve of some genus g̃ ≥ 2, with β: A_η → Jac(C_η) and α ∘ β = [d] (Poincaré reducibility); both requested from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6. The curve gives a rational map 𝔄_g ⇢ M̄_g̃.

Taking the closure of its graph (Deligne–Mumford stacks: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4) and normalising gives a first candidate J, proper over ℤ, with U its part over 𝔄_g; (a) holds by pulling back the universal stable curve, and (c) by extending α and β from the generic point with Lemma 1, Pic^τ(C/J) being semiabelian (Beispiel p. 350, requested from R11.4). Faltings covers this with 'mit Hilfe einiger trivialer Zusatzüberlegungen'.

Over U ⊗ ℚ, (d) prescribes L as the image of α^* (a line, since α^* is injective on the generic fibre), giving a rational map from U ⊗ ℚ to the projective bundle of lines in Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/J}); replacing J by the normalisation of the closure of its graph (Mathlib's relative normalisation for schemes; R09.5 for stacks) makes L a locally direct summand over all of J, so (b) and the second half of (d) hold.

For the first half of (d): the isomorphism L^{⊗r} ≅ ψ̄^*(M) is already constructed over U ⊗ ℚ; since J is normal, it suffices to extend it after base change to ℂ over one normal J̃ proper and dominant over J.

Using Namikawa's φ: N → Ā_g/ℂ one constructs a normal J̃ (for instance the normalisation of a component of J ×_{Ā_g} N dominating J) over which ψ^*(A) extends to a semiabelian scheme with ω^{⊗r} ≅ pullback of M; by Lemma 1, α and β extend over J̃, and α^* identifies the extended ω with L there, which gives the isomorphism over J̃. Faltings does not say how J̃ is built; the fibre product is the reviewers' choice.
ψ is proper because J is proper over ℤ and U is the part lying over 𝔄_g, and ψ̄ is surjective because its image is closed and contains the generic point (E4).
acceptance: Check that J is proper over Spec(Z) while A_g is not, and that the extension psibar is only claimed over Q.
Check that d in (c) is allowed to depend on the component and is only required to be nonzero; the construction produces an isogeny, not an isomorphism, between Pic^tau(C/J) and psi^*(A).
Exhibit for g = 1 the classical case (every principally polarized abelian variety of dimension 1 is its own Jacobian, d = 1).

nodes.title: Two-sided comparison e . rho^*(M) subset (omega_{A/R})^{otimes r} subset e^{-1} . rho^*(M)
nodes.statement: There is a natural number e > 0 with the following property. Let K be a number field, R its ring of integers, p : A -> Spec(R) a semiabelian variety whose generic fibre A/K is proper over K and carries a principal polarization. The corresponding map rho : Spec(K) -> A_g/Q extends to rho : Spec(R) -> Abar_g/Z, and by construction there is an isomorphism rho^*(M) otimes_R K = (omega_{A/R})^{otimes r} otimes_R K. Under this isomorphism one has e . rho^*(M) subset (omega_{A/R})^{otimes r} subset e^{-1} . rho^*(M).
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K
p : A -> Spec(R) semiabelian with A/K proper over K and principally polarized (the polarization is required only on the generic fibre)
r and M as in the previous node; e is uniform in K and in A, depending only on g

the proof begins 'Wir duerfen annehmen' that psibar : J/Q -> Abar_g/Q extends to a proper psibar : J/Z -> Abar_g/Z; this is a reduction inside the proof (for instance after replacing J by the closure of the graph), not an extra hypothesis of the Korollar (reviewer clarification)
proofSteps: 'Wir dürfen annehmen' that ψ̄ extends to a proper ψ̄: J → Ā_g/ℤ: replace J by the normalisation of the closure of the graph of ψ̄ in J ×_ℤ Ā_g/ℤ and pull back C and L; Lemma 2 still holds.

ρ: Spec(K) → A_g/ℚ extends to ρ: Spec(R) → Ā_g/ℤ by the valuative criterion, Ā_g/ℤ being projective over ℤ. Since ψ̄ is surjective and ψ̄^{−1}(A_g ⊗ ℚ) ⊆ U (E4), there are a finite extension K'/K with ring of integers R' and a lift ρ̃: Spec(R') → J whose generic point lies in U (lifting through a proper surjective morphism of Deligne–Mumford stacks after a finite extension, then the valuative criterion for the proper J: R09.4).
J is noetherian and ψ̄^*(M) ≅ L^{⊗r} over J ⊗ ℚ, so clearing denominators on a finite affine cover gives e_1 > 0 with e_1·L^{⊗r} ⊆ ψ̄^*(M) ⊆ e_1^{−1}·L^{⊗r} over J.

By Bemerkung b) it suffices to prove the claim after base change to R', comparing ω_{A/R'} and ρ̃^*(L). Pull back the stable curve q: C → Spec(R') and α, β; they are defined on the generic fibre and extend over Spec(R') by Lemma 1 (Pic^τ(C/R') is semiabelian by R11.4, A/R' by base change), with α ∘ β = [d].

ρ̃^*(L) is the saturation of α^*(ω_{A/R'}) in Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/R'}), by Lemma 2 d) and because L is a local direct summand. Since β^* α^* = [d]^* = d^g on ω_{A/R'}, and α^* β^* acts as d^g on the rank-one ρ̃^*(L) ⊗ K', one gets d^g·ρ̃^*(L) ⊆ α^*(ω_{A/R'}) ⊆ ρ̃^*(L) ('Daraus folgt unmittelbar').

Combining the two comparisons, e = e_1·d^{gr} works, with d the least common multiple of the integers of Lemma 2 c) over the finitely many components of U; e depends only on g, through J, r and M. The identifications of ρ^*(M) ⊗ K with (ω_{A/R})^{⊗r} ⊗ K agree by the second half of Lemma 2 d).

Check the failure mode: without the boundary control of Lemma 2 the isomorphism holds only over K, giving no bound at the finite places.
Test with an elliptic curve over ℚ with multiplicative reduction, where A/ℤ is the identity component of the Néron model and ρ lands in the boundary of Ā_1/ℤ.
The inclusions give |Grad(ρ^*M) − r·Grad(ω_{A/R})| ≤ [K:ℚ]·log e when the archimedean metrics agree, the bound used in Satz 1.

nodes.title: Faltings' Grad and modular height h(A), matched to the Arakelov owners
nodes.statement: Faltings' normalisation (§3, pp. 353–354) against the owners' objects. (i) A metrized line bundle on Spec(R), R = O_K, is a projective R-module P of rank 1 with norms ‖·‖_v on P ⊗_R K_v at the infinite places v; with ε_v = 1 if K_v ≅ ℝ and 2 if K_v ≅ ℂ (Mathlib's InfinitePlace.mult), Grad(P, ‖·‖) = log #(P/R·p) − Σ_v ε_v log ‖p‖_v for any p ≠ 0, independent of p by the product formula; this is the arithmetic degree of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.1. (ii) For p: A → Spec(R) semiabelian with proper generic fibre, ω_{A/R} is metrized at v by ‖α‖_v² = 2^{−g} i^{g²} ∫_{A_σ(ℂ)} α ∧ ᾱ, where A_σ = A ⊗_{K,σ} ℂ for an embedding σ inducing v (Faltings prints (i/2)^g ∫_{A(K_v)} α ∧ ᾱ: source issues E1, E2), and h(A) = Grad(ω_{A/R})/[K:ℚ] is the height of the semiabelian model in the sense of R35.3. (iii) h(A) is unchanged by base change to the ring of integers of a finite extension of K. (iv) By Lemma 1 a semiabelian model with given generic fibre is unique up to unique isomorphism, so h(A) is an invariant of A_K.
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K; ε_v = InfinitePlace.mult v
p: A → Spec(R) semiabelian with proper generic fibre A/K (properness of the generic fibre is what makes the archimedean product defined)
the metric at a real or complex place v is computed on A_σ(ℂ) for an embedding σ inducing v; it does not depend on σ, the product being invariant under complex conjugation
no polarization is required for h(A)
proofSteps: Independence of p: replacing p by xp, x ∈ K^×, adds log|N_{K/ℚ}(x)| to log #(P/R·p) and Σ_v ε_v log|x|_v = log|N_{K/ℚ}(x)| to the archimedean sum (product formula: Mathlib's NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one, with InfinitePlace.mult as ε_v); Faltings: 'die rechte Seite ist selbstverständlich unabhängig von p'.
Grad is R35.1's arithmetic degree for this normalisation: weight 2 at a complex place is the sum over its two conjugate embeddings.
The metric is Bemerkung d) with the corrected sign (E1), integrated over A_σ(ℂ) also at real places (E2).

Invariance ('Man sieht sofort'): for K'/K finite with ring of integers R', ω_{A_{R'}/R'} = ω_{A/R} ⊗_R R' (Bemerkung b)), Grad(P ⊗_R R') = [K':K]·Grad(P) (R35.1), and the metrics correspond; so h is unchanged.
(iv): Lemma 1 applied to the identity of A_K.
Faltings then compares with the usual height of points of ℙ^n(K) ('Der Name „Höhe“ rechtfertigt sich wie folgt', p. 354); that comparison is used in Lemma 3 and Satz 1.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ with semistable reduction everywhere and Néron differential ω_E (a ℤ-basis of ω_{E/ℤ}), h(E) = −(1/2)·log((i/2) ∫_{E(ℂ)} ω_E ∧ ω̄_E): minus half the logarithm of the covolume of the period lattice of ω_E.
h does not depend on the chosen nonzero p ∈ P.
With weight 1 instead of 2 at complex places Grad depends on p, and h is not invariant under field extension.
h(A) is unchanged when K is replaced by a finite extension and A by its base change.
For g = 2 the printed (i/2)^g ∫ α ∧ ᾱ is negative, so log ‖α‖_v would be undefined (E1).

nodes.title: The canonical metric on omega has logarithmic singularities along the degeneration locus
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth complex variety, Y ⊆ X a divisor with normal crossings and p: A → X a semiabelian scheme that is proper and principally polarized over X − Y. Then the canonical metric on ω_{A/X}|(X − Y) (fibrewise the product of Bemerkung d), with the corrected sign) has logarithmic singularities along Y in the sense of the definition node (with Φ the identity, locally near every point of Y). In particular (Faltings' Beispiel, proved in his [6], end of §2): taking Namikawa's φ: N → Ā_g(ℂ), with N smooth, φ^{−1}(Ā_g(ℂ) − A_g(ℂ)) a normal-crossings divisor and a semiabelian extension with ω^{⊗r} ≅ φ^*(M) (requested from ShimuraCompactifications:C2 and C4), and Φ = φ, the metric ‖·‖ on M|A_g(ℂ) induced from the Hodge metric on ω^{⊗r} has logarithmic singularities along Y = Ā_g(ℂ) − A_g(ℂ).
hypotheses: X smooth, Y a divisor with normal crossings (locally, near each point of Y)
p: A → X semiabelian, proper over X − Y, with a principal polarization over X − Y
logarithmic singularities as defined in the definition node

for the Beispiel: Namikawa's toroidal compactification N of a neat-level cover, with smooth N and normal-crossings boundary, and the semiabelian extension with ω^{⊗r} ≅ φ^*(M) (fact 2 b)); Ā_g(ℂ) itself is singular and its boundary is not a divisor with normal crossings
only a proof sketch is printed (at the referees' request); the full proof is Faltings [6], not in the library (gap)
proofSteps: Replace ω_{A/X} by the rank-g bundle s^*(Ω^1_{A/X}) of invariant differentials, whose determinant is ω_{A/X} and which equals p_*(Ω^1_{A/X}) over X − Y by Bemerkung a); Faltings writes p_*(Ω^1_{A/X}) (source issue E5). Logarithmic singularities of a hermitian vector bundle pass to its determinant (API of the definition node).

'Mit den Methoden des §2' reduce to A the Jacobian of a semistable curve q: C → X: after a proper dominant base change A is, up to the isogeny α ∘ β = [d] of Lemma 2, a factor of such a Jacobian, and α^* compares invariant differentials up to the factor d^g as in the Korollar. Faltings gives no details.

For a semistable curve q: C → D = {t : |t| < 1} with good reduction outside 0, C is covered by charts of two types: a) U_i = {(z, t) : |z| < 1, |t| < 1}, q smooth, z a fibre coordinate; b) U_i = {(z_1, z_2, t) : |z_1| < ε, |z_2| < ε, z_1 z_2 = t^m}, q = t.
A local section α of q_*(ω_{C/D}) is (holomorphic)·dz on charts of type a) and (holomorphic)·dz_1/z_1 on charts of type b).

The fibre of a chart of type b) over t is the annulus |t|^m/ε < |z_1| < ε, on which (i/2) ∫ |dz_1/z_1|² = 2π·log(ε²/|t|^m); hence (i/2) ∫_{U_i ∩ q^{−1}(t)} α ∧ ᾱ is bounded or grows at most like |log|t|| ('Eine explizite Rechnung ergibt'), and ‖·‖ ≥ (positive constant)·‖·‖_1 for a hermitian metric ‖·‖_1 on q_*(ω_{C/X}) defined on all of X.
The general case, near an arbitrary point of the normal-crossings divisor Y, 'geht genauso'; the full argument is in Faltings [6] (gap).
acceptance: Check the rate: the singularity is at most a power of |log|t||, never a power of |t|; this is exactly what Lemma 3 tolerates.
Check the elliptic case g = 1: for ℂ/(ℤ + τℤ) and q = e^{2πiτ}, ‖dz‖² = Im τ = −log|q|/(2π), so the Hodge norm of the invariant differential du/u = 2πi·dz of the Tate curve grows like |log|q||^{1/2}.
Check that the metric extends continuously over the good-reduction locus, so the singularity is concentrated along Y.

nodes.title: Finiteness of points of bounded height for a metric with logarithmic singularities
nodes.statement: Let X ⊆ ℙ^n_ℤ be Zariski closed, Y ⊆ X closed, and ‖·‖ a hermitian metric on O(1)|(X(ℂ) − Y(ℂ)), invariant under complex conjugation, with logarithmic singularities along Y (definition node). For a number field K with ring of integers R and x ∈ X(K) − Y(K), let ρ_x: Spec(R) → X extend x and put h(x) = Grad(ρ_x^*O(1), ‖·‖)/[K:ℚ], the finite places using the integral structure of O(1) and each infinite place the metric at the corresponding point of X(ℂ) − Y(ℂ). Then for every c there are only finitely many x ∈ X(K) − Y(K) with h(x) ≤ c.
hypotheses: X subset P^n_Z Zariski closed and Y subset X closed
||.|| hermitian on O(1)|(X(C) - Y(C)) with logarithmic singularities along Y in the sense of the preceding node
K a fixed number field; the statement is for K-rational points, not for points of bounded degree
proofSteps: Choose a continuous hermitian metric ‖·‖_1 on O(1)|X(ℂ) with height h_1. By R35.1's comparison, h_1 = Projectivization.logHeight + O(1) on X(K) (Faltings, p. 354: 'Bei Veränderung der hermiteschen Metrik ändert sich die Höhenfunktion nur um einen beschränkten Betrag').
Choose s > 0 and f_1, …, f_t ∈ Γ(X/ℤ, O(s)) with common zero set exactly Y: homogeneous generators of the ideal of Y, multiplied by monomials to a common degree s.

Scale ‖·‖_1 so that ‖f_i‖_1 ≤ e^{−1} on X(ℂ) (the ‖f_i‖_1 are bounded, X(ℂ) being compact). Pulling back along Φ, each Φ^*f_i is divisible by the reduced local equation f of Φ^{−1}(Y), so the definition and compactness give c_1, c_2 > 0 with |log (‖·‖/‖·‖_1)(z)| ≤ c_1 + c_2·min_i log|log ‖f_i(z)‖_1| for z ∈ X(ℂ) − Y(ℂ). Faltings prints the left side as log|(‖·‖/‖·‖_1)(z)| and does not normalise ‖f_i‖_1 (source issue E7).

For x ∈ X(K) − Y(K) choose i with ρ_x^*(f_i) ≠ 0. Then s·[K:ℚ]·h_1(x) ≥ −Σ_v ε_v log ‖f_i(x_v)‖_1 ≥ ε_v·|log ‖f_i(x_v)‖_1| for each infinite v, and summing the estimate of the previous step over the infinite places gives |h(x) − h_1(x)| ≤ c_3 + c_4·log h_1(x) for h_1(x) ≥ 1, with c_3, c_4 depending on K.

Hence h(x) ≤ c bounds h_1(x), and so logHeight(x). Northcott on ℙ^n(K): normalise a coordinate x_j = 1; each coordinate then has mulHeight₁(x_i) = mulHeight ![x_i, 1] ≤ mulHeight(x) (Mathlib's Height.mulHeight₁_div_eq_mulHeight and Height.mulHeight_comp_le), and NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le leaves finitely many choices.
acceptance: Check that the argument needs the common zero locus of the f_i to be exactly Y; a larger zero locus destroys the comparison.
Check that the estimate is only |h − h_1| ≤ c_3 + c_4 log h_1 and not a two-sided constant bound; the conclusion still follows.

On X = ℙ^1_ℤ, Y = {t = 0}, the metric ‖·‖ = ‖·‖_1·|t|^{−1} near t = 0 (a pole of order one) gives h(x_N) = h_1(x_N) − log N = O(1) for x_N = (N : 1) with t(x_N) = 1/N, so infinitely many points have bounded height: the logarithmic rate is used.

sources.match: Literal statement.

sources.excerpt: mit log|‖ ‖/‖ ‖_1 (z)| ≤ c_1 + c_2·inf{log(|log‖f_i(z)‖_1|)} für z ∈ X(ℂ). … erhält man sofort Konstanten c_3, c_4 > 0 mit |h(x) − h_1(x)| ≤ c_3 + c_4·log(h_1(x)).

nodes.title: Finiteness of extensions of bounded degree unramified outside S (imported)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and S a finite set of places of K. Then there are only finitely many field extensions K' of K of a given degree that are unramified outside S.
hypotheses: K a number field, S a finite set of places of K; the places of S may be wildly ramified, and ramification at infinite places does not affect finiteness
the degree [K' : K] is fixed
K' ranges over subfields of a fixed algebraic closure (up to isomorphism the count is also finite)
proofSteps: Faltings gives no proof: 'Bekannt (Hermite-Minkowski)'.
Let n = [K' : K]. Only primes above S divide the different of O_{K'} over O_K (Mathlib's not_dvd_differentIdeal_iff: a prime divides the different if and only if it ramifies).

At a prime P above p ∈ S with ramification index e ≤ n, v_P(different) ≤ e − 1 + v_P(e) (Serre, Local Fields III §6, remark after Proposition 13). This bound is planned by the Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic roadmap, layer 6.4, and is not in the pinned libraries: gap. It bounds the norm of the different in terms of K, S and n.
The tower formula |disc K'| = N(different)·|disc K|^n (Mathlib's NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_absNorm_differentIdeal_mul_natAbs_discr_pow) then bounds |disc K'|.
Hermite's theorem for number fields inside a fixed algebraic closure of ℚ (Mathlib's NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd) leaves finitely many K'.
acceptance: Check that the discriminant bound depends on the wild part of S: the tame estimate v_P(different) = e − 1 alone does not suffice at places above the residue characteristic; ℚ(√2)/ℚ at 2 attains e − 1 + v_P(e) = 3.

Check the uses in this paper: the descent step of Satz 1 (K' containing the 3-division points of all members of a geometric class), the finiteness transfer (K' containing K(B[12d])), Satz 5 (K' containing all extensions of degree ≤ l^{8g²} unramified outside l and S) and Satz 7 (K_1 over which the fibres φ^{−1}(x) split).
Check that Mathlib's NumberField.hermiteTheorem.finite_of_discr_bdd_of_isReal is not enough: it counts only fields with a real place.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 4. Sei K ein Zahlkörper, S eine endliche Menge von Stellen von K. Dann gibt es nur endlich viele Körpererweiterungen K′ ⊇ K von vorgegebener Ordnung, welche außerhalb von S unverzweigt sind. Beweis. Bekannt (Hermite-Minkowski).
sources.match: Literal statement and proof; the node is an imported theorem with a recorded gap.

nodes.title: Satz 1: finiteness of principally polarized semiabelian models of bounded modular height
nodes.statement: Fix g and a number field K with ring of integers R, and let c be given. Then there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of pairs consisting of (i) a semiabelian variety p: A → Spec(R) of relative dimension g with proper generic fibre A/K, and (ii) a principal polarization on A/K, such that h(A) ≤ c. (By Lemma 1 an isomorphism of pairs is the same as a K-isomorphism of the principally polarized generic fibres.)
hypotheses: K a number field with ring of integers R fixed; g fixed
A/K proper (so the generic fibre is an abelian variety) but A -> Spec(R) only semiabelian
a principal polarization on the generic fibre; the polarization degree is fixed to 1 here
isomorphism classes are over K (the passage from Kbar-classes to K-classes is part of the proof)
proofSteps: By Lemma 1 the semiabelian model of A/K is unique up to unique isomorphism, so the pairs are the K-isomorphism classes of principally polarized abelian varieties over K having a semiabelian model over R, and h(A) is an invariant of A/K (height comparison node, (iv)).

Let x ∈ A_g(K) be the moduli point of (A/K, λ) (PELModuli:M6) and ρ: Spec(R) → Ā_g/ℤ its extension; metrize M on A_g(ℂ) through M ≅ ω^{⊗r} (Baily–Borel) by the Hodge metric and put h(x) = Grad(ρ^*M, ‖·‖)/[K:ℚ]. The archimedean metrics of ρ^*M and ω_{A/R}^{⊗r} agree under the Korollar's isomorphism, and at the finite places e·ρ^*(M) ⊆ ω^{⊗r} ⊆ e^{−1}·ρ^*(M); hence |h(x) − r·h(A)| ≤ log e ('Nach dem Korollar zu Lemma 2 ist die Differenz … beschränkt').

The metric ‖·‖ on M|A_g(ℂ) has logarithmic singularities along Ā_g(ℂ) − A_g(ℂ) (log-singularity theorem, via Namikawa's N and the tensor-power API of the definition node). Lemma 3, with X = Ā_g/ℤ ⊆ ℙ^N_ℤ and Y the Zariski closure of Ā_g/ℚ − A_g/ℚ, shows that the x with h(x) ≤ r·c + log e are finitely many; A_g(K) ⊆ X(K) − Y(K) because A_g/ℚ is open in Ā_g/ℚ.

Each x ∈ A_g(K) is one K̄-isomorphism class of principally polarized abelian varieties (M6), and by the descent node each such class contains only finitely many K-isomorphism classes having a semiabelian model over R ('Wir müssen uns nun noch überlegen, …').
acceptance: Check the statement is for pairs (model, polarization): dropping the polarization the finiteness assertion is not what is proved here.
Check that the descent step needs level n ≥ 3 (−1 acts trivially on A[2]) and the finiteness of Aut(A, λ).

Check that the bad-reduction places are the same for all members of one K̄-class, which is what makes Lemma 4 applicable with a fixed S; this uses the semiabelian models (quadratic twists by ramified characters have additive reduction and are excluded).
Check the bound |h(x) − r·h(A)| ≤ log e with e the constant of the Korollar.

sources.excerpt: Satz 1. Sei c gegeben. Dann gibt es nur endlich viele Isomorphieklassen von Paaren aus i) einer semiabelschen Varietät der relativen Dimension g p: A → Spec(R) mit eigentlicher generischer Faser A/K ii) einer prinzipalen Polarisation auf A/K, für welche h(A) ≤ c gilt.

nodes.title: Lemma 5: the isogeny height formula
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, R = O_K, and let p_1: A_1 → Spec(R), p_2: A_2 → Spec(R) be semiabelian varieties (R28.1) of relative dimension g with proper generic fibres, s: Spec(R) → A_1 the zero section, and φ: A_1 → A_2 an isogeny; by Lemma 1 (R28.1 extension lemma) it suffices to give φ over K. Then φ is flat, G = Ker(φ) ⊆ A_1 is a quasi-finite flat commutative group scheme over Spec(R), φ induces an injection φ*: ω_{A_2/R} → ω_{A_1/R} with #(ω_{A_1/R}/φ*(ω_{A_2/R})) = #s*(Ω¹_{A_1/A_2}) = #s*(Ω¹_{G/R}), and h(A_2) = h(A_1) + ½·log(Grad(φ)) − (1/[K:ℚ])·log(#s*(Ω¹_{G/R})), where h is the modular height of R28.1 and Grad(φ) is the degree of the isogeny φ_K.
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K its ring of integers

A_1, A_2 semiabelian over Spec(R) of relative dimension g with proper generic fibres; ω_{A/R} = s*(Ω^g_{A/R}) is the Hodge line bundle of R28.1 with the metric ‖α‖_v² = (i/2)^g ∫ α∧ᾱ at the infinite places
φ: A_1 → A_2 an isogeny, possibly given only on generic fibres; Lemma 1 extends it over the normal base Spec(R)
Grad(φ) is the degree of φ_K; G = Ker(φ) is quasi-finite and flat over R, in general not finite
proofSteps: Extend φ, and a quasi-inverse ψ: A_2 → A_1 with ψ∘φ = [Grad(φ)] on generic fibres (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3), over Spec(R) by Lemma 1; ψ∘φ = [Grad(φ)] then holds over R because both sides agree on the schematically dense generic fibre and A_1 is separated.

Faltings asserts 'Da φ automatisch flach ist'. Flatness of φ, quasi-finite flatness of G = A_1 ×_{A_2} Spec(R) (fibre over the zero section), injectivity of φ* on invariant differentials and the identification of its cokernel with s*(Ω¹_{A_1/A_2}) = s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) are the integral half of the isogeny formula owned by ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.4 (requested); the equality s*(Ω¹_{A_1/A_2}) = s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) is the base change of Ω¹_{A_1/A_2} along the zero section of A_2.
At each infinite place, pulling back a top form along φ(ℂ), a finite map of degree Grad(φ), multiplies ∫ α∧ᾱ by Grad(φ), so φ* multiplies the norm ‖·‖_v by Grad(φ)^{1/2} (archimedean half of R35.4).

Compute Grad(ω_{A_1/R}) with the section φ*(t) for a nonzero t ∈ ω_{A_2/R}: log #(ω_{A_1}/R·φ*t) = log #(ω_{A_1}/φ*ω_{A_2}) + log #(ω_{A_2}/R·t) and Σ_v e_v log‖φ*t‖_v = Σ_v e_v log‖t‖_v + ([K:ℚ]/2)·log Grad(φ), since Σ_v e_v = [K:ℚ]; divide by [K:ℚ].
acceptance: Multiplication by n: for φ = [n] on A of relative dimension g, Grad(φ) = n^{2g}, G = A[n] and #s*(Ω¹_{A[n]/R}) = #(R/nR)^g = n^{g[K:ℚ]}, so the formula reads h(A) = h(A) + g·log n − g·log n.
At a prime 𝔭 of R not dividing Grad(φ), G is étale over R_𝔭 and contributes nothing: the finite term is supported on the primes dividing Grad(φ).
Only the generic-fibre isogeny is an input; the extension over R comes from Lemma 1.
Sign check: with ‖·‖ as in R28.1 the norm of φ*t is Grad(φ)^{1/2}·‖t‖; the opposite sign violates the multiplication-by-n check.

sources.excerpt: (Nach Lemma 1 reicht es natürlich, wenn man φ über K definiert.) Wir setzen G=Ker(φ)⊆A₁. Da φ automatisch flach ist, ist G ein quasiendliches flaches Gruppenschema über Spec(R).

nodes.title: Bemerkung: exp(2[K:Q](h(A_2) - h(A_1))) is rational with prime divisors dividing the isogeny degree
nodes.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5, let n ∈ ℕ annihilate G = Ker(φ) (n = Grad(φ) always does). Then n annihilates Ω¹_{G/R}, and exp(2[K:ℚ]·(h(A_2) − h(A_1))) = Grad(φ)^{[K:ℚ]}·(#s*(Ω¹_{G/R}))^{−2} is a rational number in whose numerator and denominator only prime divisors of Grad(φ) occur. Their exponents are bounded in terms of the exponents in Grad(φ): for every prime p, with g the relative dimension, −(2g−1)·[K:ℚ]·v_p(Grad(φ)) ≤ v_p(exp(2[K:ℚ](h(A_2) − h(A_1)))) ≤ [K:ℚ]·v_p(Grad(φ)).
hypotheses: the hypotheses of Lemma 5; g the relative dimension of A_1 and A_2
n ∈ ℕ annihilating G; n = Grad(φ) is admissible because ψ∘φ = [Grad(φ)] for a quasi-inverse ψ and G, being R-flat, is the schematic closure of its generic fibre
v_p the p-adic valuation on ℚ^×
proofSteps: For a commutative group scheme G over R, [n] induces multiplication by n on s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) (additivity of the co-Lie functor); [n] = 0 on G factors through the zero section, so n·s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) = 0, and Ω¹_{G/R} ≅ (structure map)*s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) by translation invariance.

G ⊆ A_1 is a closed subgroup, so s*(Ω¹_{G/R}) is a quotient of the rank-g locally free module s*(Ω¹_{A_1/R}); being killed by n it is a quotient of s*(Ω¹_{A_1/R})/n, of order n^{g[K:ℚ]}. Hence v_p(#s*(Ω¹_{G/R})) ≤ g[K:ℚ]·v_p(n), and it is 0 for p ∤ n.
By Lemma 5, exp(2[K:ℚ](h(A_2) − h(A_1))) = Grad(φ)^{[K:ℚ]}·(#s*(Ω¹_{G/R}))^{−2}, a rational number; take v_p and use step 2 with n = Grad(φ).
acceptance: Korollar 3 (p. 362) consumes exactly this: if for every prime l some isogeny A → B has l-part of its degree dividing N, then numerator and denominator of exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) divide N^{(2g−1)[K:ℚ]}, so h(B) is bounded.

Sharpness in [K:ℚ]: an isogeny of degree p whose kernel is étale over R gives valuation exactly [K:ℚ] > v_p(Grad(φ)) = 1 when [K:ℚ] ≥ 2, so the literal bound 'at most v_p(Grad(φ))' is false; the dual isogeny (kernel the Cartier dual μ_p, s*Ω¹ = R/pR) gives −[K:ℚ].
Multiplication by p on an elliptic curve (g = 1): Grad = p², #s*Ω¹ = p^{[K:ℚ]}, valuation 0, within [−2[K:ℚ], 2[K:ℚ]].
The statement controls which primes occur and their exponents; it gives no bound on the height difference beyond that.

nodes.title: Lemma 6: inertia acts trivially on T_l(A)/T_l(H_i)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, R = O_K, p: A → Spec(R) semiabelian with proper generic fibre, l a prime, v_i a place of K above l, K_i = K_{v_i} with valuation ring R_i, and s the closed point of Spec(R_i). Let Â be the formal group scheme over Spf(R_i) obtained by completing A/R_i along the special fibre A_s; write A_s as an extension 0 → T_s → A_s → B_s → 0 of an abelian variety B_s by a torus T_s, and lift T_s to a torus T over Spec(R_i), so that T̂ is a closed formal subscheme of Â. Put Ĥ_i = Â[l^∞]; it is the formal completion of an l-divisible group H_i over R_i, H_i/K_i is an l-divisible subgroup of A[l^∞]/K_i, and likewise for T[l^∞], giving ℤ_l-lattices T_l(T) ⊆ T_l(H_i) ⊆ T_l(A). Let D_i = Gal(K̄_i/K_i) and I_i ⊆ D_i the inertia group. Then I_i acts trivially on T_l(A)/T_l(H_i), and the induced action of D_i/I_i ≅ ℤ̂ factors through a finite quotient of ℤ̂.
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K, A/R semiabelian with proper generic fibre; v_i | l, so the residue characteristic of R_i is l
Â is the completion along the whole special fibre, not only along the zero section, so H_i also contains the étale part of the finite part of A[l^∞]
a polarization of A/K (one always exists) supplies the pairing ⟨ , ⟩: T_l(A) × T_l(A) → ℤ_l(1); it is nondegenerate but need not be perfect
the lift T of T_s uses that homomorphisms from a torus into smooth group schemes lift (the source's parenthesis on p. 358)
proofSteps: The polarization of A/K gives an alternating, D_i-equivariant, nondegenerate pairing ⟨ , ⟩: T_l(A) × T_l(A) → ℤ_l(1) = T_l(𝔾_m) (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3, requested).

Orthogonality ⟨T_l(T), T_l(H_i)⟩ = 0, cited by Faltings as SGA VII, Exp. IX, §7. In SGA 7 I, IX 7.3 (valid for every prime l, including the residue characteristic), (7.3.1) identifies the fixed part T_l(A⁰)^f with T_l(Â⁰), i.e. with T_l(H_i), and (7.3.2) its toric part T_l(A⁰)^t with T_l(T̂) ≅ T_l(T); by (7.4.2)-(7.4.3) the pairing of a biextension on the fixed parts factors through the abelian parts T_l(A)^f/T_l(A)^t, so it kills T_l(A)^t × T_l(A')^f. Taking A' the dual and composing with the polarization gives the orthogonality. Imported: the factorization rests on SGA 7 I, VIII 3.5 (unread, recorded gap); the owner in the atlas is NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3 (requested).

Ranks: by (7.3.6), 0 → T_l(A⁰)^t → T_l(A⁰)^f → T_l(B) → 0, T_l(H_i) has rank t + 2b = 2g − t (t = dim T_s, b = dim B_s), and T_l(T) has rank t; T_l(H_i) is saturated in T_l(A) because H_i/K_i is an l-divisible subgroup. With nondegeneracy, T_l(H_i) = T_l(T)^⊥ ('Aus Dimensionsgründen').
x ↦ ⟨x, ·⟩ restricted to T_l(T) induces an injective D_i-linear map T_l(A)/T_l(H_i) → Hom_{ℤ_l}(T_l(T), ℤ_l(1)).

Hom_{ℤ_l}(T_l(T), ℤ_l(1)) ≅ X*(T) ⊗ ℤ_l, X*(T) the character group; T splits over the unramified extension of K_i given by a finite extension of the residue field over which T_s splits, so I_i acts trivially and D_i/I_i ≅ ℤ̂ through a finite quotient (toric part and character group: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.2, requested).
acceptance: Good reduction (T_s = 0): T_l(H_i) = T_l(A), the quotient is 0 and the lemma is empty.

Tate curve E_q over K_i (B_s = 0, t = 1): T_l(T) = ℤ_l(1) = T_l(H_i), and T_l(E_q)/ℤ_l(1) ≅ ℤ_l with trivial action for split multiplicative reduction and the unramified quadratic character for non-split reduction.
The conclusion concerns the quotient only: on T_l(E_q) itself inertia acts through a nontrivial unipotent matrix when l ∤ v(q).
The orthogonality ⟨T_l(T), T_l(H_i)⟩ = 0 is the imported SGA 7 input, not a consequence of the definitions used here.

sources.excerpt: Ĥ_i=Â[l^∞] die assoziierte l-divisible Gruppe. Ĥ_i ist formale Komplettierung einer l-divisiblen Gruppe H_i über R_i, und H_i/K_i ist eine l-divisible Untergruppe von A[l^∞]/K_i. Dasselbe gilt für T[l^∞], und zu diesen Untergruppen gehören ℤ_l-Untergitter T_l(T)⊆T_l(H_i)⊆T_l(A).

nodes.title: Local differential count for an l-divisible group over R_i (Tate, Proposition 2, as applied on p. 359)
nodes.statement: Let K_i be a finite extension of ℚ_l of degree m_i with valuation ring R_i, and let Γ be an l-divisible group over R_i whose maximal formal (connected) subgroup has dimension d. Then for every n ≥ 0, #s*(Ω¹_{Γ[l^n]/R_i}) = l^{n·m_i·d}. Consequently, if A → A' is an isogeny of semiabelian schemes over R_i whose quasi-finite flat kernel has finite part (the open and closed subgroup scheme that is finite over R_i and contains the unit section) equal to Γ[l^n], then #s*(Ω¹_{A/A'}) = l^{n·m_i·d}. In Faltings' notation (p. 359), with Γ = G_i: #(s*Ω¹_{A/A_n} ⊗_R R_i) = #s*(Ω¹_{(G_i)_n/R_i}) = l^{n·m_i·d_i}; by the erratum, the hypothesis that the finite part of the kernel is (G_i)_n holds only after the shift of the R28.3 nodes.
hypotheses: K_i/ℚ_l finite of degree m_i, R_i its valuation ring (complete, residue characteristic l), so #(R_i/lR_i) = l^{m_i}
Γ an l-divisible group over R_i of height h' and dimension d (the dimension of its connected part Γ⁰, a formal Lie group), 0 ≤ d ≤ h'
for the consequence: an isogeny of semiabelian schemes over R_i whose kernel's finite part is Γ[l^n]
proofSteps: Tate's Proposition 2 ([13] in Faltings), in the form Faltings uses: the invariant differentials of Γ[l^n] form a free R_i/l^n R_i-module of rank d, so #s*(Ω¹_{Γ[l^n]/R_i}) = #(R_i/l^n R_i)^d = l^{n·m_i·d}. Imported: Tate's paper is not available (gap); the local term is requested from ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.4, whose stage text supplies 'the inequalities and local terms that R28 uses'.

A quasi-finite separated flat group scheme G' over the henselian ring R_i is the disjoint union of an open and closed subgroup G'^f, finite over R_i and containing the unit section, and a part with empty special fibre; hence s*(Ω¹_{G'/R_i}) = s*(Ω¹_{G'^f/R_i}) (finite part: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1, requested).
For the isogeny A → A' with kernel G', the cokernel of the pull-back on invariant differentials is s*(Ω¹_{A/A'}) = s*(Ω¹_{G'/R_i}) as in Lemma 5, so its order is #s*(Ω¹_{Γ[l^n]/R_i}) = l^{n·m_i·d}.
acceptance: Étale Γ (d = 0), e.g. (ℚ_l/ℤ_l)^{h'}: the count is 1.
Multiplicative Γ = μ_{l^∞}^{h'} (d = h'): s*(Ω¹_{μ_{l^n}}) = R_i/l^n, count l^{n·m_i·h'}.
d is the dimension of the connected part, not the height: for E[l^∞] of an elliptic curve with good ordinary or supersingular reduction h' = 2 and d = 1, count l^{n·m_i}.
The local degree m_i must appear: for K_i ramified over ℚ_l, #(R_i/lR_i) = l^{m_i}, not l^{f_i}.

nodes.title: The determinant identity Σ_i m_i d_i = mh/2
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree m = [K:ℚ] with ring of integers R, A/K an abelian variety with a semiabelian model over R, l a prime, and G ⊆ A[l^∞] an l-divisible subgroup over K of height h. Let v_1, …, v_r be the places of K above l, m_i = [K_{v_i}:ℚ_l] (so Σ_i m_i = m), and suppose that for every i hypothesis (H_i) of the Hodge-Tate determinant lemma holds: V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) = V_l(Γ_i) for an l-divisible group Γ_i over R_i of dimension d_i. Then Σ_{i=1}^r m_i d_i = mh/2. The proof uses π = Gal(K̄/K) ⊆ π̃ = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), W̃ = Ind_π^π̃ T_l(G) ⊆ Ṽ = Ind_π^π̃ T_l(A) (rank mh), and the character χ: π̃ → ℤ_l^× through which π̃ acts on the line L = Λ^{mh}(W̃) ⊆ Λ^{mh}(Ṽ).
hypotheses: m = [K:ℚ] = Σ_i m_i with m_i = [K_{v_i}:ℚ_l] over the places v_i | l
A/K has a semiabelian model over R, so Lemma 6 applies at every v_i; G/K ⊆ A[l^∞]/K is l-divisible of height h

(H_i) for every i: V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) = V_l(Γ_i) for an l-divisible group Γ_i over R_i of dimension d_i. Faltings takes Γ_i = G ∩ H_i for A itself; by the erratum this holds only after replacing A by A_m, m large, which is how the corrected Satz 2 applies this node (V_l(G), V_l(H_i) and the identity are unchanged by the passage)
proofSteps: Induction (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1): W̃ = Ind_π^π̃ T_l(G) ⊆ Ṽ = Ind_π^π̃ T_l(A) has rank mh, and π̃ acts on L = Λ^{mh}(W̃) through a continuous character χ: π̃ → ℤ_l^×.
By the character lemma (Kronecker-Weber), χ = ⟨χ_0⟩^a·ε with a ∈ ℤ_l and ε of finite order, χ_0 the l-adic cyclotomic character (mathlib cyclotomicCharacter).
By the determinant lemma at l, L ⊗_{ℤ_l} C ≅ C(Σ_i m_i d_i) as modules over the decomposition group D ≅ Gal(ℚ̄_l/ℚ_l), C the completion of ℚ̄_l.

Tate's Theorem 2 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2, requested): χ·χ_0^{−Σ m_i d_i} has finite image on the inertia group I ⊆ D. Since χ·χ_0^{−Σ m_i d_i} = ⟨χ_0⟩^{a − Σ m_i d_i}·(character of finite order) and ⟨χ_0⟩(I) is open in 1 + qℤ_l, this forces a = Σ m_i d_i, so χ·χ_0^{−Σ m_i d_i} has finite order on π̃, hence on D.

By the Frobenius-weight lemma, for almost all p, χ(F_p) is an algebraic number all of whose conjugates have absolute value p^{mh/2}. As χ_0(F_p) = p, χ(F_p) = ζ·p^{Σ m_i d_i} with ζ a root of unity; comparing absolute values gives Σ_i m_i d_i = mh/2.
acceptance: Local degrees matter: K quadratic, l inert, E/K with good supersingular reduction at l, G = E[l^∞] (h = 2): one place, m_1 = 2, d_1 = 1, and Σ m_i d_i = 2 = mh/2; without m_i the identity fails.
Whole Tate module with good reduction: G = A[l^∞], Γ_i = A[l^∞] over R_i, d_i = g, and Σ_i m_i g = mg = m·(2g)/2.
CM check: E with CM by an imaginary quadratic field F in which l = 𝔩𝔩̄ splits, K = F, G = E[𝔩^∞] (h = 1): d = 1 at one place above l and d = 0 at the other, so Σ m_i d_i = 1 = mh/2.
Three imported inputs: Kronecker-Weber (through the character lemma), Tate's Theorem 2, and Weil's bound (through the Frobenius-weight lemma).

sources.excerpt: Wir müssen also zeigen, daß Σ m_i d_i=½mh. Dazu betrachten wir die absolute Galois-Gruppe π̃=Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), und den π̃-Modul Ṽ=Ind_π^π̃(T_l(A)) (π=Gal(K̄/K)). Dieser enthält den Untermodul W̃=Ind_π^π̃(T_l(G)) vom Rang mh

nodes.title: Erratum (a): the Zariski closures form an l-divisible group only after passing to A_m
nodes.statement: Let A, l, v_i, K_i, R_i, D_i and Â be as in Lemma 6, and let W ⊆ T_l(Â) be a D_i-invariant sublattice. It corresponds to an l-divisible subgroup of A/K_i, and taking the Zariski (schematic) closures of its levels gives a system of finite flat group schemes G_{i,n} ⊆ Â over Spf(R_i), equivalently over Spec(R_i). This system is an l-divisible group only if the maps G_{i,n+1}/G_{i,n} → G_{i,n}/G_{i,n−1} are isomorphisms for all n ≥ 1, which cannot be expected in general. A consideration of discriminants shows that they are isomorphisms for all n ≥ n_0, for some n_0. Passing from A = A_0 to A_m means that only the maps with n > m have to be considered, so for m ≥ n_0 the closures attached to A_m form an l-divisible group over R_i.
hypotheses: the setting of Lemma 6 and of the proof of Satz 2; W ⊆ T_l(Â) a D_i-invariant sublattice (in the application, W = T_l(G/G_m) ∩ T_l(Â_m) after the shift of erratum b))
G_{i,n} ⊆ Â the schematic closure over Spf(R_i) of the n-th level of the l-divisible subgroup of A/K_i attached to W
the condition is for all n ≥ 1 (printed 'n ≧ 1'); after passing to A_m only n > m matters
proofSteps: The generic l-divisible group attached to W lies in H_i ⊗ K_i; the schematic closures G_{i,n} of its levels in the finite flat H_i[l^n] (equivalently in Â) are finite flat over the discrete valuation ring R_i, with G_{i,n} ⊆ G_{i,n+1} and multiplication by l mapping G_{i,n+1} into G_{i,n} (closure of a generic finite flat subgroup: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1, requested).

The maps G_{i,n+1}/G_{i,n} → G_{i,n}/G_{i,n−1} are isomorphisms on generic fibres; the system is an l-divisible group exactly when they are isomorphisms over R_i for all n ≥ 1, which can fail at finitely many levels.

Faltings: 'lehrt eine Betrachtung der Diskriminanten, daß dies für große n der Fall ist', referring to Tate, p-divisible groups, p. 182. The erratum gives no further argument and Tate's paper is unread (gap), so the existence of n_0 is imported.

Passing from A = A_0 to A_m (the global quotient by G_m, extended over R by Lemma 1), only the maps with n > m occur; for m ≥ n_0 the closures form an l-divisible group over R_i. This is the tail the R28.3 stage asks to construct.
acceptance: The defect sits in finitely many levels only: from n_0 on the tail is l-divisible.
Degenerate case W = T_l(Â): the closures are the levels H_i[l^n] themselves, the maps are isomorphisms for all n ≥ 1, and n_0 = 1.
Nothing is claimed for A_0: the roadmap forbids asserting that the original closure tower is l-divisible.

nodes.title: Erratum (b): the intersection G intersect H_i is l-divisible only after a shift
nodes.statement: In the proof of Satz 2, the intersection G_i = G ∩ H_i of l-divisible groups over Spec(R_i) does not in general define an l-divisible group, even over K_i. The problem disappears on passing to a suitable A_m: there is m_1 such that for m ≥ m_1 the intersection (G/G_m) ∩ H_i^{(m)} inside A_m[l^∞] over K_i (H_i^{(m)} the l-divisible group of Lemma 6 for A_m) is an l-divisible group over K_i, whose rational Tate module is V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) ⊆ V_l(A) = V_l(A_m). One then continues as in a).
hypotheses: the notation of Lemma 6 and of the proof of Satz 2: G/K ⊆ A[l^∞] an l-divisible subgroup, H_i with Ĥ_i = Â[l^∞]
the defect is already at the level of K_i, not only over R_i
V_l(A_m) is identified with V_l(A) through the isogeny A → A_m
proofSteps: Over K_i the K̄_i-points of G[l^∞] and H_i[l^∞] are the images of V_l(G) and V_l(H_i) in V_l(A)/T_l(A). Their intersection is ((V_l(G) + T_l(A)) ∩ (V_l(H_i) + T_l(A)))/T_l(A), whose maximal divisible subgroup is (V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) + T_l(A))/T_l(A). The quotient is finite and can be nonzero: in (ℚ_l/ℤ_l)² the l-divisible subgroups with Tate modules ℤ_l(1,0) and ℤ_l(1,l) meet in a group of order l. So G ∩ H_i need not be l-divisible.

For A_m: T_l(A_m) = T_l(A) + l^{−m}T_l(G), the Tate module of G/G_m ⊆ A_m[l^∞] is l^{−m}T_l(G), and V_l(H_i^{(m)}) = V_l(H_i), because the isogeny φ: A → A_m over R_i (Lemma 1) and ψ with ψ∘φ = [l^m] (A3) map the formal l-divisible groups into each other.

Reviewer's argument (Faltings gives none): put Q = V_l(G) ∩ (V_l(H_i) + T_l(A)). Its image in V_l(G)/(V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i)) embeds in the finitely generated ℤ_l-module T_l(A)/(T_l(A) ∩ V_l(H_i)), so it lies in l^{−m}·(image of T_l(G)) for all m ≥ m_1. For such m, every point of (G/G_m) ∩ H_i^{(m)} lies in (V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) + T_l(A_m))/T_l(A_m), so the intersection equals its maximal divisible subgroup, an l-divisible group over K_i with rational Tate module V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i).
One continues as in a) with W = T_l(G/G_m) ∩ T_l(Â_m) ('Man kann dann wieder wie in a) weitermachen'); the two thresholds are combined in the R28.3 differential-count node.
acceptance: The defect of b) is at the level of K_i and independent of the closure defect of a): both shifts are needed, and m is taken at least both thresholds.
Good reduction at v_i: H_i = A[l^∞] over R_i, the intersection is G itself and m_1 = 0.
Toy lattice case: with T_l(A) = ℤ_l², V_l(H_i) = ℚ_l(1,l) and T_l(G) = ℤ_l(1,0), the defect has order l for m = 0 and vanishes for m ≥ 1.
No statement is made about A_0 itself.

sources.excerpt: b) Der Durchschnitt G_i=G∩H_i von l-divisiblen Gruppen über Spec(R_i) definiert im Allgemeinen nicht einmal über K_i eine l-divisible Gruppe. Auch dieses Problem verschwindet beim Übergang zu einem passenden A_m. Man kann dann wieder wie in a) weitermachen.

nodes.title: Satz 2 as corrected: the sequence h(A_n) becomes stationary
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, R = O_K, p: A → Spec(R) a semiabelian variety with proper generic fibre, l a prime, and G/K ⊆ A[l^∞]/K an l-divisible subgroup of height h. Let G_n be the kernel of l^n on G and A_n = A/G_n the semiabelian variety over R with generic fibre A_K/G_n. Then the sequence h(A_n) becomes stationary: there is m_0 with h(A_n) = h(A_{m_0}) for all n ≥ m_0. The printed conclusion h(A_n) = h(A) for all n is false (N. Katz observed the error, O. Gabber constructed a counterexample).
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K; A/R semiabelian with proper generic fibre; each A_n has a semiabelian model because semistable reduction is invariant under isogeny (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3)
l a prime; G/K ⊆ A[l^∞]/K an l-divisible subgroup defined over K, of height h
m_0 is not effective: it comes from the two shifts of the erratum
proofSteps: Choose m_0 as in the differential count along the shifted tower (both erratum shifts). Replacing A by A_{m_0} changes neither V_l(G), V_l(H_i) nor the Galois modules, and (A_{m_0})_n = A_{m_0+n}.

For n ≥ 0, A_{m_0} → A_{m_0+n} is an isogeny of degree l^{nh}. Lemma 5 and the differential count give h(A_{m_0+n}) − h(A_{m_0}) = ½·log l^{nh} − (1/m)·log l^{n Σ_i m_i d_i} = n·log(l)·(h/2 − (1/m)·Σ_i m_i d_i), m = [K:ℚ]; this is the formula printed on p. 359, valid only after the shift.
The d_i are dimensions of l-divisible groups Γ_i over R_i with V_l(Γ_i) = V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i), so hypothesis (H_i) of the determinant identity holds for A_{m_0}, and Σ_i m_i d_i = mh/2.
Hence h(A_{m_0+n}) = h(A_{m_0}) for all n ≥ 0. The Zusatz bei der Korrektur (p. 366) and the erratum both say this weaker conclusion suffices for the rest of the paper.
acceptance: Stationarity, not constancy: any consumer needing h(A_n) = h(A_0) uses a false statement (Gabber's counterexample).
What the consumer needs is boundedness: h(A_n) ≤ max(h(A_0), …, h(A_{m_0})) for all n.
G = A[l^∞]: A_n = A/A[l^n] ≅ A, so the sequence is constant, consistent with the corrected statement.
The shifts come before the height computation: the formula of step 2 is applied only to A_{m_0} → A_{m_0+n}.

nodes.title: From stationarity and Satz 1: infinitely many A_n are isomorphic
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, R = O_K, π = Gal(K̄/K), A/K an abelian variety of dimension g with a principal polarization λ that extends to a semiabelian variety over Spec(R), and l a prime. Let W ⊆ T_l(A) ⊗ ℚ_l be a π-invariant subspace that is maximal isotropic for the nondegenerate alternating form of λ, G ⊆ A[l^∞] the l-divisible subgroup over K with T_l(G) = W ∩ T_l(A), and A_n = A/G_n. Then G, the G_n, the A_n and the isogenies A → A_n are defined over K, each A_n carries a principal polarization λ_n over K, the heights h(A_n) are bounded (corrected Satz 2), and therefore, by Satz 1, infinitely many of the (A_n, λ_n) are isomorphic over K.
hypotheses: A/K principally polarized with a semiabelian model over R; both are arranged by the polarization reduction and the invariance lemma
W ⊆ V_l(A) π-invariant and maximal isotropic (dim W = g); π-invariance puts G, the G_n and the isogenies over K, maximal isotropy makes the A_n principally polarized
Satz 1 is applied with the fixed K, dimension g and polarization degree 1; the isomorphisms it gives are K-isomorphisms
proofSteps: T_l(G) = W ∩ T_l(A) is a π-stable saturated lattice of rank g; the corresponding l-divisible subgroup G ⊆ A[l^∞] and its levels G_n = G[l^n] ≅ T_l(G)/l^n T_l(G) are defined over K.

G_n has order l^{ng} and is isotropic for the pairing e^{l^n λ} on ker(l^n·λ) = A[l^n] (order l^{2ng}), because W is isotropic; so it is maximal isotropic. By descent of polarizations (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3, requested; Milne, Abelian Varieties, Prop. 13.8 and Rem. 13.9), l^n·λ = φ_n^∨ ∘ λ_n ∘ φ_n for a polarization λ_n of A_n of degree l^{2ng}/(l^{ng})² = 1, defined over K by uniqueness.
A_n has a semiabelian model over R (isogeny invariance of semistable reduction, R11.3). By the corrected Satz 2, h(A_n) is stationary, hence bounded.
Satz 1 gives finitely many K-isomorphism classes of principally polarized (A_n, λ_n) with bounded height, so infinitely many are K-isomorphic.
acceptance: Maximal isotropy, not π-invariance alone, keeps the polarizations principal: for isotropic W with dim W < g the descended polarization of A_n has degree l^{2n(g − dim W)}, unbounded, and Satz 1 with fixed degree no longer applies.
Elliptic curves (g = 1): every line is maximal isotropic, so a π-stable line of V_l(E) gives the tower; when V_l(E) is irreducible there is no such W.
The isomorphisms are over K: Satz 1 counts K-isomorphism classes, not K̄-classes.
The consumer (Satz 3 and Satz 4 after Zarhin) needs infinitely many isomorphic A_n, not h(A_n) = h(A).

nodes.title: The polarization reduction: an isogeny of degree √d to a principally polarized abelian variety after a finite extension
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K with a polarization λ of degree d. There are a finite extension L/K, a subgroup H ⊆ ker(λ)_L that is maximal isotropic for the pairing e^λ on ker(λ), and a principal polarization μ on B = A_L/H with λ_L = π^∨ ∘ μ ∘ π for the quotient isogeny π: A_L → B, of degree √d. After a further finite extension, B has a semiabelian model over the ring of integers. Together with the invariance of Satz 3 and Satz 4 under finite extension and isogeny, this is how Faltings may assume that A/K is principally polarized and extends to a semiabelian variety over Spec(R).
hypotheses: A/K an abelian variety over a number field with a polarization λ of degree d (every abelian variety over K has one; d is a square)
L/K finite with ker(λ) constant over L; any L over which some maximal isotropic H is defined suffices
semistable reduction after a further finite extension: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3

the source states the reduction in one sentence on p. 361, and uses the same construction in the proof of Korollar 3 ('eine Isogenie vom Grad √d mit einer prinzipal polarisierten abelschen Varietät', p. 362)
proofSteps: ker(λ) is a finite étale group scheme of order d over K, and e^λ: ker(λ) × ker(λ) → μ is alternating and nondegenerate (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3), so d is a square and maximal isotropic subgroups have order √d.
Choose L/K finite with all points of ker(λ) rational over L and a maximal isotropic H ⊆ ker(λ)(L); then B = A_L/H and π are defined over L (Tau Ceti base change and isogenies).

Descent of polarizations (A3, requested; statement read in Milne, Abelian Varieties, 2008 notes, Prop. 13.8, over an algebraically closed field, degree prime to the characteristic, automatic here): since H ⊆ ker(λ) is isotropic, λ = π^∨ ∘ μ ∘ π for a polarization μ of B, unique because π is an isogeny; uniqueness makes μ Galois-invariant, hence defined over L. By Milne, Rem. 13.9, deg λ = deg μ·(deg π)², so deg μ = 1.
After a further finite extension, B has semistable reduction everywhere, i.e. a semiabelian model over the ring of integers (R11.3, requested).
Zarhin's trick ((A × A^∨)^4 principally polarized) is not needed, because the ground field may be enlarged; it is needed only when it may not.
acceptance: This is where the roadmap's 'Zarhin's trick or the appropriate polarisation argument' enters: in Faltings it is a single sentence on p. 361, justified by the field extension, not by Zarhin's trick.
The quaternion construction on T_l(A)^8 (R28.4) is a different construction: it needs the principal polarization already in place, and the product polarization on A^8.
Korollar 3 (p. 362) uses the same degree √d.

tests.name: PolarizationReduction.not_whole_kernel

nodes.title: Zarhin's quaternion construction: a maximal isotropic W_1 in V_l(A)^8 built from an arbitrary invariant subspace W
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional ℚ_l-vector space with a nondegenerate alternating form e, and let a group π act on V by similitudes of e (e(σx, σy) = c(σ)·e(x, y) for a character c); for V = V_l(A) = T_l(A) ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l of a principally polarized abelian variety A this is the Weil pairing and c is the l-adic cyclotomic character. Let a, b, c, d ∈ ℚ_l with a² + b² + c² + d² = −1 and let v be the matrix of left multiplication by the quaternion a + bi + cj + dk in the basis 1, i, j, k, v = [[a, −b, −c, −d], [b, a, d, −c], [c, −d, a, b], [d, c, −b, a]], so that v·ᵗv = (a² + b² + c² + d²)·1 = −1. Give V^4 = V ⊗ ℚ_l^4 and V^8 = V^4 × V^4 the orthogonal-sum forms and let v act on V^4 through the factor ℚ_l^4. For a π-invariant subspace W ⊆ V with orthogonal complement W^⊥ put W_1 = {(x, vx) : x ∈ W^4} ⊕ {(y, −vy) : y ∈ (W^⊥)^4} ⊆ V^8. Then W_1 is π-invariant and maximal isotropic (dim W_1 = 4·dim V = ½·dim V^8), and the ℚ_l-linear map V^8 → V^4, (s, t) ↦ ½(s + v⁻¹t), maps W_1 onto W^4. For V = V_l(A), V^8 = V_l(A^8) and the orthogonal-sum form is the Weil pairing of the product principal polarization of A^8.
hypotheses: a, b, c, d ∈ ℚ_l with a² + b² + c² + d² = −1, as printed ('Wähle a, b, c, d ∈ ℚ_l'); such a quadruple exists for every prime l, even in ℤ_l (node minus-one-is-a-sum-of-four-squares-in-Q_l)
e nondegenerate and alternating on V; π acts by similitudes of e, so W^⊥ is π-invariant whenever W is
W an arbitrary π-invariant ℚ_l-subspace of V (not assumed isotropic); W^⊥ its orthogonal complement for e
the scalar matrix v acts on V^4 = V ⊗ ℚ_l^4 through the second factor, so it commutes with the diagonal action of π
proofSteps: Direct multiplication gives v·ᵗv = (a² + b² + c² + d²)·1 = −1, hence ᵗv·v = −1 and v is invertible with v⁻¹ = −ᵗv.
For x, x' ∈ V^4 and a scalar 4 × 4 matrix u, e(ux, x') = e(x, ᵗu·x'). Hence e((x, vx), (x', vx')) = e(x, x') + e(x, ᵗv·v·x') = 0 and e((y, −vy), (y', −vy')) = 0.
Cross terms: e((x, vx), (y, −vy)) = e(x, y) − e(x, ᵗv·v·y) = 2·e(x, y) = 0, because x ∈ W^4 and y ∈ (W^⊥)^4 are componentwise orthogonal. So W_1 is isotropic.

The sum is direct: (x, vx) = (y, −vy) forces x = y and 2vx = 0, so x = 0. With dim W + dim W^⊥ = dim V (nondegeneracy; Mathlib's finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal) this gives dim W_1 = 4·dim W + 4·dim W^⊥ = 4·dim V = ½·dim V^8, so W_1 is maximal isotropic.
π acts diagonally and commutes with v, and W, W^⊥ are π-invariant, so W_1 is π-invariant.

Every element of W_1 is (x + y, v(x − y)) with x ∈ W^4, y ∈ (W^⊥)^4, and ½((x + y) + v⁻¹v(x − y)) = x; so (s, t) ↦ ½(s + v⁻¹t) maps W_1 onto W^4. The node every-invariant-subspace-is-the-image-of-an-idempotent uses this map to bring the idempotent back from A^8 to A.
acceptance: The coefficients are required only in ℚ_l, as printed; a quadruple with a² + b² + c² + d² = −1 exists at l = 2 (b = c = 1, d = 2, a² = −7, a 2-adic square because −7 ≡ 1 mod 8) as well as at odd l.
The dimension count dim W_1 = 8g = ½·dim V_l(A^8) is derived from dim W + dim W^⊥ = 2g, not assumed.
The recovery map (s, t) ↦ ½(s + v⁻¹t) sends W_1 onto W^4, so no information about W is lost in passing to A^8.

nodes.title: Satz 3 and Satz 4: semisimplicity of V_l(A) and End_K(A) otimes Z_l = End_pi(T_l)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A/K an abelian variety of dimension g, l a prime and T_l = T_l(A) the Tate module with its action of π = Gal(K̄/K). Satz 3: the action of π on T_l ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l is semisimple. Satz 4: the natural map End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_l → End_π(T_l) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: K a number field; A/K an abelian variety; l an arbitrary prime, l = 2 included
End_K(A) is the ring of endomorphisms defined over K
the two statements are proved together; Satz 4 is first reduced to the rational statement that End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l → End_π(T_l ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l) is bijective ('Es reicht bekanntlich')
one may enlarge K and replace A by an isogenous variety (node reduction-to-a-principally-polarized-semiabelian-model), so A may be assumed principally polarized with a semiabelian model over Spec(R)
proofSteps: Integral from rational ('Es reicht bekanntlich'): End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l → End(T_l) is injective with torsion-free cokernel (A6; Milne, Abelian Varieties, I Theorem 10.15). If the rational map is onto End_π(V_l), then for f ∈ End_π(T_l) some l^k·f lies in the image of End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l, hence so does f; injectivity is part of the same statement.
Reduce to A principally polarized with a semiabelian model over Spec(R) (node reduction-to-a-principally-polarized-semiabelian-model).

By the quaternion transfer node every π-invariant subspace of V = V_l(A) is e(V) for an idempotent e ∈ E = End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l, and every π-invariant subspace of V ⊕ V = V_l(A × A) is the image of an element of End_K(A × A) ⊗ ℚ_l = M_2(E).
Satz 3: for a π-invariant W = e(V), W' = (1 − e)(V) is a complement, and it is π-invariant because π commutes with E.

Rational Satz 4: for α ∈ End_π(V) the graph Γ = {(x, αx)} is π-invariant in V ⊕ V, so Γ = u(V ⊕ V) with u ∈ M_2(E). Each c in the centralizer C of E in End(V) gives diag(c, c), which commutes with M_2(E) and so maps Γ into Γ; hence αc = cα. So α lies in the double centralizer of E, which is E because E is semisimple (Tau Ceti centralizer_centralizer_range).
Faltings attributes the idempotent step and the rest of the proof to Zarhin [16]; the steps above are that argument as written out in Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Theorem 2.5.
acceptance: Injectivity and surjectivity of End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l → End_π(T_l) are both established, not an equality of dimensions.
The statement is for End_K: for E/ℚ: y² = x³ − x, which has complex multiplication by ℤ[i] over ℚ(i), End_ℚ(E) = ℤ and End_π(T_l(E)) = ℤ_l, although End_ℚ̄(E) has rank 2.
The integral statement follows from the rational one only through the torsion-freeness of the cokernel of End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l → End(T_l).

nodes.title: Korollar 1 to Satz 4: Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗ ℤ_l ≅ Hom_π(T_l(A_1), T_l(A_2))
nodes.statement: Let A_1, A_2 be abelian varieties over the number field K and l a prime. Then the natural map Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_l → Hom_π(T_l(A_1), T_l(A_2)) is an isomorphism; tensoring with ℚ_l, Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l ≅ Hom_π(V_l(A_1), V_l(A_2)).
hypotheses: A_1, A_2 abelian varieties over the number field K; l any prime
Hom_K(A_1, A_2) is the group of homomorphisms defined over K (in Tau Ceti the commutative group of homomorphisms of abelian varieties, written multiplicatively)
proofSteps: Apply Satz 4 to A_1 × A_2: End_K(A_1 × A_2) ⊗ ℤ_l → End_π(T_l(A_1) ⊕ T_l(A_2)) is an isomorphism.

Both sides are 2 × 2 block matrices: End_K(A_1 × A_2) has blocks End A_1, Hom(A_2, A_1), Hom(A_1, A_2), End A_2 by the universal property of the product, and T_l(A_1 × A_2) = T_l(A_1) ⊕ T_l(A_2) (R01.6). The map respects the blocks, so its (2,1) block Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗ ℤ_l → Hom_π(T_l(A_1), T_l(A_2)) is an isomorphism.
Tensor with ℚ_l over ℤ_l for the rational form.
acceptance: For A_1 = A_2 = A the statement is Satz 4.
For non-isogenous A_1, A_2 both sides vanish; e.g. for the elliptic curves 37a1 and 37b1 over ℚ (a_2 = −2 and 0 respectively), Hom_π(T_l, T_l') = 0.
The target is the π-equivariant homomorphisms, not all ℤ_l-linear maps.

nodes.title: Korollar 3: finiteness of d-fold polarized B with T_l(A) = T_l(B) for all l
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A/K an abelian variety and d > 0. Then there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of d-fold polarized abelian varieties B/K such that T_l(A) ≅ T_l(B) as π-modules for every prime l.
hypotheses: K a number field; A/K an abelian variety; d > 0 the fixed polarization degree
the hypothesis is a π-isomorphism T_l(A) ≅ T_l(B) for every prime l simultaneously

in the proof one enlarges K and reaches: (a) all B have semistable reduction, (b) all B/K are principally polarized, (c) there is an N such that for every prime l and every B there is an isogeny φ : A → B whose largest l-power factor of Grad(φ) divides N
proofSteps: For each l, lift a π-isomorphism T_l(A) → T_l(B) through Korollar 1 to f ∈ Hom_K(A, B) ⊗ ℤ_l and approximate it l-adically by φ ∈ Hom_K(A, B) with φ ≡ f mod l; then T_l(φ) is an isomorphism, so φ is an isogeny of degree prime to l (the l-part of deg φ is the index of T_l(φ)(T_l A) in T_l B, R01.6). This is 'Die Voraussetzung besagt, daß zu jedem l eine Isogenie vom Grad prim zu l zwischen A und B existiert'.

Every such B has good reduction exactly where A has (R11.5), so the finiteness reduction applies with S the bad places of A: over a finite extension K' independent of B, A and all B are semiabelian over R', and each (B, λ) is replaced by a principally polarized (B', λ') isogenous to it by an isogeny of degree √d, with finite fibres. This gives (a), (b), and (c) with N = √d (compose A → B, of degree prime to l, with B → B', of degree √d).

The Bemerkung after Lemma 5, applied for each l to an isogeny as in (c), shows that no prime l ∤ N occurs in exp(2[K':ℚ](h(B') − h(A))) and bounds the exponent of each l | N in terms of N, g and [K':ℚ]. So this rational number lies in a finite set and the h(B') are bounded.
Satz 1 over K' gives finitely many (B', λ'), hence by the finiteness reduction finitely many (B, λ) over K.
acceptance: The conclusion is finiteness of isomorphism classes of d-fold polarized abelian varieties over K; the polarization is part of the data.
The proof uses the hypothesis for every l (it supplies, for each l, an isogeny of degree prime to l); from a single l this height bound is not available.
The height bound comes from the Bemerkung after Lemma 5 and condition (c), not from Northcott alone.

nodes.title: Satz 5: finitely many isogeny classes of abelian varieties of given dimension with good reduction outside S
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and S a finite set of places of K. Then there are only finitely many isogeny classes of abelian varieties of a prescribed dimension g over K having good reduction outside S.
hypotheses: K a number field, S a finite set of places of K, g fixed
good reduction outside S
the proof fixes an auxiliary prime l and uses the finite Galois extension K' of K containing all extensions of K of degree ≦ l^{8g²} unramified outside l and S (Lemma 4)
the places v_1, …, v_r must lie outside S and not above l, so that F_v and L_v are defined; the source leaves this implicit (source issue)
the ℤ_l-algebra M generated by the image of π in End_{ℤ_l}(T_l(A_1)) × End_{ℤ_l}(T_l(A_2)) is free of rank ≦ 8g² = (2g)² + (2g)²
proofSteps: For v ∉ S, L_v(A, s)^{−1} is det(1 − Nv^{−s}F_v | T_l(A)), whose characteristic polynomial has integer coefficients (R01.6) and roots of absolute value Nv^{1/2} (Weil, R34.2); so it is one of finitely many polynomials (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1/weil-polynomials-finite, degree 2g, weight 1, q = Nv). 'Nach den Weil-Vermutungen gibt es für v ∉ S nur endlich viele Möglichkeiten für den lokalen L-Faktor.'
Fix a prime l. The representations V_l(A) of abelian varieties of dimension g with good reduction outside S are unramified outside S and the places above l (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, R11.5).

Frobenius test set (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1/frobenius-test-set, with T the finite places in S together with those above l, d = 2g, so 2d² = 8g²): there are finitely many places v_1, …, v_r outside T such that two such representations with equal Frobenius traces at the v_i have equal traces on all of π. This is exactly Faltings' argument: K' from Lemma 4, the v_i chosen by Chebotarev to cover the conjugacy classes of G = Gal(K'/K), M free of rank ≦ 8g², ρ : π → (M/lM)^* with #(M/lM)^* ≦ l^{8g²} factoring through G, and Nakayama.

If A_1, A_2 have the same local factors at v_1, …, v_r, their Frobenius traces agree there, so tr(σ | V_l(A_1)) = tr(σ | V_l(A_2)) for all σ ∈ π. Both are semisimple (Satz 3), so V_l(A_1) ≅ V_l(A_2) (trace criterion), and Korollar 2, (ii) ⇒ (i), makes A_1 and A_2 isogenous. This last step is not printed: the proof on p. 363 ends with the generation of M/lM.
So the isogeny class is determined by (L_{v_1}, …, L_{v_r}), which takes finitely many values.
acceptance: v_1, …, v_r depend only on g, K, S and the auxiliary prime l, and the conclusion concerns isogeny classes, not isomorphism classes.
The rank bound 8g² for M and #(M/lM)^* ≦ l^{8g²} (as printed; in fact <, since 0 is not a unit) is what forces ρ to factor through G.
Nakayama is applied to the finitely generated ℤ_l-module M over the local ring ℤ_l.

nodes.title: The auxiliary polynomials P_h(T) and the choice of N
nodes.statement: Let n be the product of the primes l at which either K/Q is ramified or A does not have good reduction at all places of characteristic l. Choose a prime p not dividing n, put pitilde = Gal(Qbar/Q), pi = Gal(Kbar/K), and for 0 <= h <= 2 g m (g = dim A, m = [K:Q]) set P_h(T) = det[T - F_p | Lambda^h(Ind_pi^pitilde(T_l(A)))], where l is a prime coprime to p n and F_p is the Frobenius at p. The P_h(T) are independent of l, have coefficients in Z, and their roots have absolute value p^{h/2} (Weil). Choose N >= 2 so large that no prime l > N divides P_h(+- p^j) whenever 0 <= h <= 2 g m, 0 <= j <= g m and j != h/2; also require N >= n p.
hypotheses: A/K an abelian variety of dimension g over the number field K of degree m = [K:ℚ]
n the product of the primes l at which K/ℚ is ramified or A fails to have good reduction at some place of characteristic l
p a prime not dividing n; l a prime not dividing p·n; F_p a Frobenius at p in π̃ = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), well defined up to conjugacy because Ind_π^{π̃}(T_l(A)) is unramified at p
the absolute value p^{h/2} (printed p^{+h/2}) is Weil's theorem for abelian varieties over finite fields (R34.2)
the printed exclusion 'j ‡ ½h' is j ≠ h/2 in the journal's typography
proofSteps: Since p ∤ n, K/ℚ is unramified at p and A has good reduction at every place v | p. F_p permutes the cosets π̃/π in orbits corresponding to the places v | p, of lengths f_v = [k_v : 𝔽_p], and on the block of Ind_π^{π̃}(T_l(A)) belonging to v, F_p^{f_v} acts as a Frobenius F_v of K at v. Hence det(T − F_p | Ind T_l(A)) = ∏_{v | p} det(T^{f_v} − F_v | T_l(A)). (Equivalently Ind T_l(A) = T_l(Res_{K/ℚ} A), AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6.)

det(T − F_v | T_l(A)) has integer coefficients independent of l (R01.6) and roots of absolute value (Nv)^{1/2} = p^{f_v/2} (Weil, R34.2). So P_1 has integer coefficients independent of l and roots α_1, …, α_{2gm} of absolute value p^{1/2}.
P_h(T) = ∏_{|I| = h} (T − ∏_{i ∈ I} α_i): its coefficients are integer symmetric polynomials in the α_i, hence integers independent of l, and its roots have absolute value p^{h/2}.

For j ≠ h/2, |±p^j| = p^j ≠ p^{h/2}, so P_h(±p^j) is a nonzero integer; there are finitely many pairs (h, j), so finitely many primes divide these integers, and N is chosen above all of them and ≥ np.
acceptance: The exclusion j ≠ h/2 is exactly where the Weil bound is used; without it P_h(±p^j) can vanish and no N exists.
P_h has integer coefficients independent of l, so the divisibility condition is a condition on integers.
For K = ℚ and an elliptic curve with good reduction at p: P_0 = T − 1, P_1 = T² − a_p·T + p, P_2 = T − p; for 11a1 and p = 2, P_1 = T² + 2T + 2.

sources.excerpt: Dazu sei n das Produkt der Primzahlen l, für welche entweder die Erweiterung K⊇ℚ in l verzweigt, oder A nicht gute Reduktion an allen Stellen der Charakteristik l hat. Wähle eine Primzahl p, welche n nicht teilt.

sources.excerpt: P_h(T)=det[T−F_p|Λ^h(Ind_π^{π̃}(T_l(A)))]. Dabei ist l eine zu pn prime Primzahl … Die P_h(T) sind unabhängig von l, haben Koeffizienten in ℤ, und ihre Nullstellen haben absoluten Betrag p^{+h/2} (Weil-Vermutung oder besser -Satz).

sources.excerpt: Wir wählen nun N≧2 so groß, daß keine Primzahl l>N P_h(±p^j) teilt, falls 0≦h≦2gm, 0≦j≦gm, j‡½h. Außerdem sei N≧np.
