nodes.title: χ·ε^h = χ_0^d: Raynaud's determinant computation for the kernel of an isogeny killed by l > N
nodes.statement: Let B_1, B_2 be abelian varieties over K isogenous to A, all with semistable reduction everywhere, and φ : B_1 → B_2 an isogeny whose kernel G is killed by a prime l > N (so l ∤ n: K/ℚ is unramified at l and B_1 has good reduction at every place above l). Let l^h = deg φ, V_l = T_l(B_1)/l·T_l(B_1) ≅ B_1[l](K̄), Ṽ_l = Ind_π^{π̃}(V_l), W_l = G(K̄), W̃_l = Ind_π^{π̃}(W_l) ⊆ Ṽ_l, χ : π̃ → (ℤ/lℤ)^* the character of π̃ on L = Λ^{mh}(W̃_l) ⊆ Λ^{mh}(Ṽ_l), ε as in the node on unramifiedness, and l^d = #s^*(Ω^1_{G/R}) for the closure G of the kernel in the semiabelian model (0 ≦ d ≦ gm). Then χ·ε^h = χ_0^d.
hypotheses: B_1 has semistable reduction everywhere and good reduction above l (l > N ≥ np ≥ n)
K/ℚ is unramified at l, so every completion K_v, v | l, has absolute ramification index e = 1 ≦ l − 1, as Raynaud's Théorème 4.1.1 requires
G is finite flat over R_v for v | l and étale over the other places, so s^*(Ω^1_{G/R}) is supported above l and is a quotient of ω_{B_1/R}/l, whence 0 ≦ d ≦ gm
Raynaud's section 4 works over a strictly henselian base of unequal characteristics (p. 271); the theorem is applied after base change to the strict henselization of R_v

the exponent in Raynaud is v(𝔇̄(𝒢)), the valuation of the absolute different (appendix, Définition 8, p. 279); its identification with the length of s^*(Ω^1_{G/R_v}) is not stated in either source (gap)
proofSteps: χ·ε^h is unramified outside l (node twisted-determinant-character-is-unramified-outside-l), hence χ·ε^h = χ_0^k for some k (node mod-l-characters-unramified-outside-l-are-cyclotomic-powers).

Let I ⊆ π̃ be an inertia group at l. As K/ℚ is unramified at l, I fixes every coset of π̃/π, so by the transfer formula of the unramifiedness node χ·ε^h(σ) = ∏_t det(t⁻¹σt | W_l) for σ ∈ I, the product over coset representatives t; for each place v | l exactly f_v of the t⁻¹σt lie in an inertia group I_v of K at v.

Raynaud's Théorème 4.1.1, for G over the strict henselization of R_v (e = 1 ≦ l − 1), says that I_v acts on det(W_l) through the tame character τ_l^{v(𝔇̄(G_v))}, and τ_l is χ_0 restricted to inertia. Since χ_0 is a character of π̃, χ_0(t⁻¹σt) = χ_0(σ).
Hence χ·ε^h = χ_0^{d'} on I with d' = Σ_{v|l} f_v·v(𝔇̄(G_v)), and d' = log_l #s^*(Ω^1_{G/R}) = d once the absolute different of G_v is identified with the Fitting ideal of s^*(Ω^1_{G_v/R_v}) (gap).
χ_0 maps I onto 𝔽_l^* (ℚ(ζ_l)/ℚ is totally ramified at l), so χ_0^k = χ_0^d on I forces k ≡ d mod (l − 1): χ·ε^h = χ_0^d.
acceptance: l > N ≥ np forces K/ℚ unramified at l, so Raynaud's hypothesis e ≦ l − 1 holds with e = 1; the argument is invalid without it.
The global identity follows from the local one only through unramifiedness outside l, class field theory over ℚ, and the surjectivity of χ_0 on inertia at l.
For K = ℚ and G ≅ μ_l locally at l, h = d = 1 and χ = χ_0 on inertia at l (det of μ_l is μ_l, and #s^*(Ω^1_{μ_l/ℤ_l}) = l); for G étale at l, d = 0 and χ·ε^h = 1.

sources.excerpt: Diese Potenz läßt sich mit Hilfe von [10], Théorème 4.11 (statt der Tateschen Theorie [13]) wie folgt bestimmen: Sei l^d=#s*(Ω¹_{G/R}), 0≦d≦gm. Dann ist (nach Raynaud) χ·ε^h=χ_0^{+d}.

nodes.title: Finitely many isomorphism classes of π-stable lattices in a semisimple ℚ_l-representation (local Jordan–Zassenhaus)
nodes.statement: Let T be a free ℤ_l-module of finite rank with a continuous action of a group π such that V = T ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l is a semisimple ℚ_l[π]-module, and let M_l be the ℤ_l-subalgebra of End_{ℤ_l}(T) generated by π. Then the π-stable ℤ_l-lattices in V fall into finitely many isomorphism classes of π-modules (equivalently, of M_l-modules).
hypotheses: V semisimple; for V = V_l(A) this is Satz 3. It makes M_l ⊗ ℚ_l a semisimple ℚ_l-algebra, since a finite-dimensional algebra with a faithful semisimple module is semisimple
the finiteness is a local Jordan–Zassenhaus theorem for lattices over the ℤ_l-order M_l; the source asserts it in one sentence and gives no proof
the R28.1 stage text requires this finite-lattice theorem to be proved in this roadmap or its general-algebra owner identified; no atlas stage owns it
proofSteps: M_l ⊗ ℚ_l is semisimple because V is a faithful semisimple module over it.
M_l is contained in a maximal ℤ_l-order M' of M_l ⊗ ℚ_l, and l^k·M' ⊆ M_l for some k (both are lattices in M_l ⊗ ℚ_l).
For a π-stable lattice Λ, M'Λ is an M'-lattice with l^k·M'Λ ⊆ Λ ⊆ M'Λ.

Over a maximal order in a semisimple algebra over the complete discretely valued field ℚ_l, a lattice is determined up to isomorphism by the module it spans, so every M'Λ is isomorphic to a fixed Λ_0, and Λ is isomorphic to one of the finitely many M_l-submodules between l^k·Λ_0 and Λ_0.

The two inputs of the last three steps (a maximal order containing M_l; lattices over a maximal order over a complete discrete valuation ring determined by their span) are not proved in any source read here and are recorded as a gap.
acceptance: The statement is about lattices up to isomorphism of π-modules, not up to equality or homothety; for trivial π on ℚ_l² every lattice is isomorphic to ℤ_l².

Semisimplicity is necessary: for π = {[[1, x], [0, 1]] : x ∈ ℤ_l} acting on ℚ_l², the lattices ℤ_l e_1 ⊕ l^k ℤ_l e_2 (k ≥ 0) are π-stable and pairwise non-isomorphic, since every π-automorphism of V is [[α, β], [0, α]] and preserves the relative position of Λ ∩ ℚ_l e_1 and the image of Λ in V/ℚ_l e_1.
The only input from Satz 3 is the semisimplicity of V.

sources.excerpt: Es reicht also, wenn es nur endlich viele Isomorphie-Klassen π-invarianter Gitter in T_l(A)⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l gibt. Dazu sei M_l die von π erzeugte ℤ_l-Unteralgebra von End_{ℤ_l}(T_l(A)). Es folgt dann alles aus der Tatsache, daß M_l⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l halbeinfach ist (Satz 3).

nodes.title: Satz 6 (Shafarevich conjecture): finiteness of d-polarized abelian varieties with good reduction outside S
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places of K and d > 0. Then there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of d-fold polarized abelian varieties over K of a prescribed dimension having good reduction outside S.
hypotheses: K a number field, S a finite set of places of K, d > 0, dimension g fixed
in the proof one reduces to a single isogeny class (Satz 5), assumes all B extend to semiabelian varieties over Spec(R) and takes d = 1

the reduction to d = 1 and to semiabelian models is the finiteness reduction; 'wie im Beweis des Korollar 3' is not literally the same argument, because uniformity of the field extension now comes from good reduction outside S and Lemma 4 (source issue)
proofSteps: By Satz 5 the B/K under consideration fall into finitely many isogeny classes; fix one, with representative A.
By the finiteness reduction one may pass to a finite extension K' (independent of B) and assume that A and all B extend to semiabelian varieties over Spec(R) and that d = 1.

exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) is a rational number (Bemerkung after Lemma 5). For l > N its l-part is 1: split an isogeny A → B into an l-primary part and a part of degree prime to l; the first preserves h (node on isogenies of large prime-power degree) and the second contributes no l (Bemerkung). For each of the finitely many l ≦ N the l-part takes finitely many values (node on small primes).
So exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) lies in a finite set, the h(B) are bounded, and Satz 1 gives finitely many (B, principal polarization) over K', hence finitely many d-polarized B over K.
acceptance: Check that the polarization degree d is fixed and the reduction to d = 1 is part of the proof, not an extra hypothesis on consumers.
Check that the finiteness is of isomorphism classes of polarized abelian varieties over K, and that the good-reduction hypothesis is outside a fixed finite S.
Check that no naive projective height bound is used: the height bound is produced by the two arguments above, exactly as the roadmap text demands.

nodes.title: Korollar 1 to Satz 6: finiteness of curves of genus at least 2 with good reduction outside S
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places of K and g ≥ 2. There are only finitely many isomorphism classes of smooth curves X/K (projective and geometrically connected) of genus g with good reduction outside S.
hypotheses: K, S fixed; the genus g ≥ 2 is fixed (the printed 'vom Geschlecht g≧2' uses the dimension g of Satz 6)
'Kurve' means a smooth projective geometrically connected curve
good reduction of X at v gives good reduction of its Jacobian at v (Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Proposition 4.1)

the proof is the single word 'Torelli'; what is used is the rational Torelli theorem (for g ≥ 2 over a perfect field the isomorphism class of X is determined by that of the principally polarized Jacobian; Milne IV Theorem 4.2), imported (gap)
proofSteps: X ↦ (J(X), θ_X), θ_X the canonical principal polarization, sends curves of genus g with good reduction outside S to principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g with good reduction outside S.
Satz 6 with d = 1 gives finitely many such (J, θ) up to K-isomorphism.
By the rational Torelli theorem (g ≥ 2, K perfect) the map is injective on K-isomorphism classes, so there are finitely many X.
acceptance: Only injectivity of X ↦ (J(X), θ_X) on K-isomorphism classes is used; whether a principally polarized abelian variety is a Jacobian over K (the quadratic-twist question for non-hyperelliptic curves) is not needed.
Good reduction of X implies good reduction of J(X); the converse is not used.
g ≥ 2 is needed for the rational Torelli theorem: a curve of genus 1 without a K-point is not determined by its Jacobian (Milne IV Exercise 4.4).

nodes.title: Satz 7 (Mordell conjecture) from Shafarevich finiteness via the Parshin construction
nodes.statement: Let X/K be a smooth curve of genus g >= 2. Then X(K) is finite.
hypotheses: K a number field; X/K a smooth (projective, geometrically connected) curve of genus g ≥ 2

after a possible extension of the ground field there is an unramified covering φ : X_1 → X of degree m > 2 (printed 'vom Grad m>2', confirmed on the page image); with m > 2, D = φ^{−1}(x) − {y} has at least two points, so the generalized Jacobian of (X_1, D) has a nontrivial torus part and the double covering Y(x) → X_1 is ramified over D

Lemma 4 supplies a finite extension K_1 of K such that for every x ∈ X(K), φ^{−1}(x) consists of m distinct K_1-rational points (the fibres are étale over the ring of S-integers for a fixed S, and have degree m)
Y(x) has bad reduction only at places dividing 2, places of bad reduction of X_1, and places where φ ramifies mod v

implicit in 'Dasselbe gilt für die Abbildung Y(x) → X_1 → X': de Franchis' theorem (finitely many nonconstant maps from a fixed curve to X of genus ≥ 2; Milne IV Theorem 5.2), genus(Y(x)) ≥ 2 (Riemann–Hurwitz), and a field of definition of Y(x) independent of x (source issue)
placement: HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.4 owns the Parshin construction; this node records Faltings' version and does not realise R28.5
proofSteps: This is Parshin's argument ([9]). After a possible extension of the ground field there is an unramified covering φ : X_1 → X of degree m > 2.
Lemma 4 gives a finite extension K_1 of K such that for each x ∈ X(K) the fibre φ^{−1}(x) consists of m distinct K_1-rational points; choose one, y ∈ φ^{−1}(x) (printed 'y ∈ p^{−1}(x)', a misprint).
Let D = φ^{−1}(x) − {y} and let A/K_1 be the generalized Jacobian of (X_1, D). Using y one constructs a map X_1 − D → A.

Multiplication by 2 on A induces a covering Y(x) → X_1 ramified exactly over D; Y(x) can have bad reduction only at places v of K_1 with (a) v | 2, (b) X_1 bad at v, or (c) φ ramified in the fibre mod v.

These are finitely many places, so by Korollar 1 there are finitely many possibilities for Y(x) (Y(x) has genus ≥ 2 by Riemann–Hurwitz), and by de Franchis finitely many possibilities for the map Y(x) → X_1 → X, which is ramified exactly over x.
Hence X(K) is finite.
acceptance: The construction attaches to each x ∈ X(K) a curve Y(x) in a finite set and a map Y(x) → X ramified exactly over x, which determines x.
The three bad-reduction conditions keep the bad set of Y(x) inside a fixed finite set.
The degree m > 2 is what makes D contain at least two points; with m = 2 the covering Y(x) → X_1 would be unramified.

sources.locator: Section 6, Satz 7 and the start of its proof, p. 365

nodes.title: Bemerkung 2: for almost all l the algebra generated by pi is the full commutant of End_K(A) otimes Z_l
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A/K an abelian variety. For almost all primes l, the ℤ_l-subalgebra M_l of End_{ℤ_l}(T_l(A)) generated by π is the full commutant of End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_l in End_{ℤ_l}(T_l(A)). Faltings states that this follows from Satz 6 by the method of Zarhin [16].
hypotheses: K a number field, A/K an abelian variety
M_l the Z_l-algebra generated by the image of pi in End_{Z_l}(T_l(A))
the conclusion is for almost all l, not for all l
the method is quoted from Zarhin [16]; Faltings gives no proof here
proofSteps: Faltings records this as Bemerkung 2 at the end of Section 6 and deduces it from Satz 6 'mit Hilfe der Methode aus [16]'; no proof is printed and none is read here (gap).

The rational analogue holds for every l and follows from Satz 3 and Satz 4 by the double centralizer theorem: the ℚ_l-span of the image of π in End(V_l(A)) is the centralizer of End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l (Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Corollary 2.7). The integral statement for almost all l is the refinement that needs Satz 6.
For an elliptic curve E/ℚ (End_ℚ(E) = ℤ) it says that for almost all l the image of π generates M_2(ℤ_l) as a ℤ_l-algebra, so E[l] is an irreducible 𝔽_l[π]-module for almost all l.
acceptance: The assertion is integral (over ℤ_l) and holds for almost all l; the exceptional set is not made explicit here.
It differs from Satz 4, which identifies End_π(T_l) with End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l for every l, by describing the algebra generated by π rather than its commutant.
For E/ℚ with complex multiplication (e.g. y² = x³ − x) and l unramified in ℚ(i), the image of π is the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup, which still generates M_2(ℤ_l).

nodes.title: Hermitian metrics with logarithmic singularities along a closed subvariety
nodes.statement: Let X be a compact complex variety (the analytification of a proper ℂ-scheme), Y ⊆ X a closed subvariety, M a line bundle on X and ‖·‖ a continuous hermitian metric on M|(X − Y). The metric has logarithmic singularities along Y if there are a proper dominant morphism Φ: X̃ → X with X̃ smooth and Φ^{−1}(Y) a divisor with normal crossings, and constants c_1, c_2 > 0, such that on a neighbourhood of every point of Φ^{−1}(Y), for a local generator h of Φ^*(M) and a local equation f of Φ^{−1}(Y) with |f| ≤ 1/2, sup{‖h‖, ‖h‖^{−1}} ≤ c_1·|log|f||^{c_2}. The bound is required only near Φ^{−1}(Y) (source issue E6). For a hermitian vector bundle the same definition applies with ‖h‖ and ‖h‖^{−1} the operator norms of a local frame and of its inverse.
hypotheses: X compact (proper over ℂ), Y ⊆ X closed; M a holomorphic line bundle on X (analytification of an algebraic one)
‖·‖ continuous on M|(X − Y); nothing is assumed near Y beyond the displayed bound
the bound is local: it is required near each point of Φ^{−1}(Y), where |f| < 1 (read literally at a point where a local equation has |f| = 1 the printed inequality cannot hold: E6)
proofSteps: Define the predicate on (X, Y, M, ‖·‖) as stated; the resolution Φ and the constants are existentially quantified, as in Faltings' Definition (p. 355).

Independence of the local choices: changing h or f by a unit changes both sides by bounded factors on a smaller neighbourhood; Φ^{−1}(Y) is compact, so finitely many neighbourhoods and one pair of constants suffice.
acceptance: The metric of M on A_g(ℂ) used in Satz 1 satisfies the definition along Ā_g(ℂ) − A_g(ℂ) with Φ Namikawa's φ: N → Ā_g(ℂ) (log-singularity theorem).

uses.how: the hypothesis on the metric of O(1)|(X(ℂ) − Y(ℂ)) in Lemma 3, in the form of the log-ratio estimate
the conclusion of the log-singularity theorem for the Hodge metric
transported from ω^{⊗r} on Namikawa's N to M on Ā_g(ℂ) through Φ = φ

nodes.title: Descent: finitely many K-forms with semiabelian models in one geometric isomorphism class
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with ring of integers R and (A_0, λ_0) a principally polarized abelian variety over K. Then there are only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of principally polarized abelian varieties (A, λ) over K such that A has a semiabelian model over Spec(R) and (A, λ) ⊗_K K̄ ≅ (A_0, λ_0) ⊗_K K̄.
hypotheses: K a number field, R = O_K, K̄ an algebraic closure
each A has a semiabelian model over Spec(R), i.e. semistable reduction at every finite place; without this the statement is false
isomorphisms respect the principal polarizations
proofSteps: Every such A has semistable reduction at all finite places. For semistable A, good reduction at v is equivalent to potentially good reduction at v, which depends only on A ⊗ K̄; so all members have good reduction outside the same finite set S ('Es ist bekannt, daß alle diese an denselben Stellen von K schlechte Reduktion haben'; requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.6).

Fix n = 3. For each member, K(A[3]) is Galois over K with group inside GL_{2g}(ℤ/3), hence of degree ≤ #GL_{2g}(𝔽_3), and unramified outside S ∪ {v | 3} by Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (R11.6). By Lemma 4, applied for each degree up to that bound, only finitely many such fields occur; let K' be the Galois closure of their compositum ('für ein n ≥ 3 die Koordinaten der n-Teilungspunkte aller A/K').

If (A, λ), (B, μ) are members and f: (A, λ)_{K̄} → (B, μ)_{K̄} an isomorphism, then for σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K') the automorphism f^{−1} ∘ σ(f) of (A, λ)_{K̄} is trivial on A[3], since σ fixes A[3] and B[3] pointwise; by Serre's rigidity (level n ≥ 3; PELModuli:M2) it is the identity, so f is defined over K' ('Bekanntlich sind dann unsere A's schon über K' isomorph').

Fixing one member (A, λ), every member is a K-form of (A, λ) split by K'; these are classified by H^1(Gal(K'/K), Aut_{K'}(A, λ)) (PELModuli:M6), a finite set since Gal(K'/K) and Aut(A, λ) are finite (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6): 'der Rest folgt aus allgemeinen Grundsätzen der Galois-Kohomologie'.
acceptance: g = 1: the members of a geometric class are twists of one elliptic curve; a quadratic twist by a character ramified at a place of good or multiplicative reduction has additive reduction there, so semistability everywhere leaves finitely many twists.
Level 2 does not rigidify: −1 acts trivially on A[2].
Without semiabelian models the set is infinite: the quadratic twists of an elliptic curve over ℚ by all squarefree integers are pairwise non-isomorphic over ℚ and isomorphic over ℚ̄.

sources.excerpt: Wir müssen uns nun noch überlegen, daß nur endlich viele K-Isomorphieklassen dieselbe Klasse über dem algebraischen Abschluß K̄ induzieren können. Wir fixieren also eine solche Klasse über K̄, und betrachten die entsprechenden A/K.

nodes.title: Principal polarization after a uniform extension, and the finiteness transfer to d-fold polarizations
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of finite places of K and g, d ≥ 1. There is a finite Galois extension K'/K, depending only on K, S, g and d, with the following properties. (i) For every abelian variety B/K of dimension g with good reduction outside S and every polarization μ of B of degree d, B_{K'} has semistable reduction at every place of K', ker μ is a constant group scheme over K', and for every subgroup H ⊆ ker μ maximal isotropic for the Weil pairing e^μ the quotient π: B_{K'} → B' = B_{K'}/H is an isogeny of degree √d onto a principally polarized (B', μ') with π^*μ' = μ_{K'}, again with semistable reduction everywhere and good reduction outside the places above S. (ii) If, for a set 𝒮 of K-isomorphism classes of such pairs (B, μ), the principally polarized (B', μ') of (i) lie in finitely many K'-isomorphism classes, then 𝒮 is finite.
hypotheses: K a number field, S a finite set of finite places, g ≥ 1, d ≥ 1 (the degree #ker μ of a polarization is a square)
B/K abelian of dimension g with good reduction outside S; μ a polarization of degree d
no height bound is assumed: heights enter only when (ii) is combined with Satz 1 and Lemma 5
proofSteps: K(B[12d]) is Galois over K of degree ≤ #GL_{2g}(ℤ/12d), unramified outside S ∪ {v | 12d} (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich; R11.6). By Lemma 4 finitely many such fields occur; K' is the Galois closure of their compositum. Over K', B has semistable reduction everywhere by Grothendieck's criterion (semistable over K(B[m]) at places prime to m, m ≥ 3, used with m = 3 and m = 4; R11.6), and ker μ ⊆ B[d] is constant.

Over K', e^μ is a non-degenerate alternating pairing on ker μ; a maximal isotropic H has order √d, and μ descends to a principal polarization μ' on B' = B_{K'}/H with π^*μ' = μ_{K'} (Mumford, Abelian Varieties §23; requested from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3). Good and semistable reduction pass to the isogenous B' (R11.6).

Conversely, with π': B' → B_{K'} the isogeny such that π' ∘ π = [d], B_{K'} ≅ B'/π(B[d]) with π(B[d]) a K'-rational subgroup of B'[d]; B'[d] has finitely many subgroups, π is determined by π' (π ∘ π' = [d]), and μ_{K'} = π^*μ'. So each (B', μ') gives finitely many (B, μ)_{K'} up to K'-isomorphism.

Each (B, μ) in 𝒮 is then a K-form, split by K', of one of finitely many polarized abelian varieties over K'; such forms are classified by H^1(Gal(K'/K), Aut_{K'}(B, μ)) (PELModuli:M6), finite because Gal(K'/K) and Aut(B, μ) are finite (A6). Hence 𝒮 is finite.

This is the argument behind Faltings' 'eine Isogenie vom Grad √d mit einer prinzipal polarisierten abelschen Varietät' (proof of Korollar 3, p. 362) and 'daß d = 1 ist' (proof of Satz 6, p. 363), which the source does not spell out. It is the polarisation argument and finiteness transfer the R28.1 stage asks for; Zarhin's trick is not needed because S is fixed, so Lemma 4 makes K' uniform, and no lattices over orders in semisimple algebras occur.
acceptance: For d = 1 the lemma is empty: H = 0, B' = B_{K'}, and (ii) is the descent of K'-forms.

For an elliptic curve (g = 1) every polarization is a multiple m·λ_0 of the principal one, of degree m², with ker = B[m]; a maximal isotropic H has order m (for m = p² one choice is B[p], giving B' ≅ B).
Without a fixed S no uniform K' exists (the fields K(B[d]) are unbounded), which is why Satz 1's bounded-height finiteness is stated for principal polarizations only.

nodes.title: Hodge-Tate determinant at a place above l: Λ^h V_l(G) ⊗ C_i ≅ C_i(d_i)
nodes.statement: Let A, l, v_i, K_i, R_i, H_i, D_i be as in Lemma 6, G ⊆ A[l^∞] an l-divisible subgroup over K of height h, and C_i the completion of an algebraic closure of K_i. Suppose (H_i): the D_i-stable subspace W_i = V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) of V_l(A) = T_l(A) ⊗ ℚ_l is the rational Tate module V_l(Γ_i) of an l-divisible group Γ_i over R_i of height h_i and dimension d_i. Then Λ^h V_l(G) ⊗_{ℚ_l} C_i ≅ C_i(d_i) = C_i(χ_0^{d_i}) as semilinear D_i-modules, χ_0 the l-adic cyclotomic character.
hypotheses: the setting of Lemma 6; G/K ⊆ A[l^∞]/K l-divisible of height h
(H_i) as stated; Faltings takes Γ_i = G ∩ H_i, which by erratum b) and a) is an l-divisible group over R_i only after replacing A by A_m, m large
C_i(k) = C_i ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℤ_l(k), with D_i acting diagonally and semilinearly
proofSteps: Tate's Hodge-Tate decomposition ([13], Theorem 3, Corollary 2): V_l(Γ_i) ⊗ C_i ≅ C_i^{h_i−d_i} ⊕ C_i(1)^{d_i} as D_i-modules (imported; requested from HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0).

U = V_l(G)/W_i injects D_i-equivariantly into V_l(A)/V_l(H_i), on which by Lemma 6 I_i acts trivially and D_i through a finite quotient; so D_i acts on U through a finite quotient, and U ⊗ C_i ≅ C_i^{h−h_i} (a representation with finite image is C_i-trivial: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2, requested).
Determinants are multiplicative in 0 → W_i → V_l(G) → U → 0, so Λ^h V_l(G) ⊗ C_i ≅ Λ^{h_i}(W_i ⊗ C_i) ⊗ Λ^{h−h_i}(U ⊗ C_i) ≅ C_i(d_i).
acceptance: Étale case d_i = 0 (for instance G étale at v_i): the determinant is C_i-trivial.
Multiplicative case: for the l-divisible group of the torus of a Tate curve over K_i (h = 1), W_i = V_l(G), d_i = 1 and the determinant is C_i(1).
The twist is +1 per formal dimension (Tate's 'C_i^{d_i}(+1)'); with the opposite sign the determinant identity would read Σ m_i d_i = −mh/2, impossible for h > 0.

sources.excerpt: Wenn C_i die Komplettierung des algebraischen Abschlusses von K_i bezeichnet, so ist weiter bekannt ([13], Theorem 3, Corollary 2), daß T_l(G_i)⊗_{ℤ_l}C_i≅C_i^{h_i−d_i}⊕C_i^{d_i}(+1), (h_i=Höhe(G_i), „(+1)“=Tate-Twist) als D_i-Moduln.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 359; the imported Hodge-Tate decomposition.

sources.excerpt: Zusammen mit Lemma 6 ergibt sich daraus, daß D_i auf Λ^h T_l(G)⊗_{ℤ_l}C_i⊆Λ^h T_l(A)⊗_{ℤ_l}C_i (h=Höhe(G)) wie auf C_i(χ_0^{d_i})=C_i(d_i) operiert (χ_0=zyklotomischer Charakter).

nodes.title: l-adic characters of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) are l-adic powers of the cyclotomic character up to finite order
nodes.statement: Let l be a prime, χ_0: Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) → ℤ_l^× the l-adic cyclotomic character, q = l for l odd and q = 4 for l = 2, and for x ∈ ℤ_l^× let ⟨x⟩ ∈ 1 + qℤ_l be its component in ℤ_l^× = μ(ℤ_l) × (1 + qℤ_l). For every continuous homomorphism χ: Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) → ℤ_l^× there are a unique a ∈ ℤ_l and a character ε of finite order with χ = ⟨χ_0⟩^a·ε. For k ∈ ℤ, χ·χ_0^{−k} has finite order if and only if a = k.
hypotheses: l a prime; χ continuous for the profinite topology on Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) and the l-adic topology on ℤ_l^×
no ramification hypothesis on χ is needed
the base field is ℚ: over other number fields there are further ℤ_l-extensions, which is why Faltings induces to ℚ first
proofSteps: χ factors through Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)^ab. By Kronecker-Weber (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, 'kroneckerWeber', requested), ℚ^ab = ⋃_n ℚ(μ_n), and by mathlib IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.galEquivZMod, Gal(ℚ^ab/ℚ) ≅ lim_n (ℤ/n)^× = ∏_p ℤ_p^×, with ℤ_l^×-component χ_0 (mathlib cyclotomicCharacter).

⟨χ⟩ restricted to ∏_{p≠l} ℤ_p^× is a continuous homomorphism into the torsion-free pro-l group 1 + qℤ_l. It kills each factor ℤ_p^× (pro-p part with p ≠ l, and finite torsion), hence the dense subgroup ⊕_{p≠l} ℤ_p^×, so it is trivial.
A continuous endomorphism of 1 + qℤ_l ≅ ℤ_l is x ↦ x^a for a unique a ∈ ℤ_l, and ⟨·⟩ kills the torsion of ℤ_l^×; hence ⟨χ⟩ = ⟨χ_0⟩^a, and ε = χ·⟨χ_0⟩^{−a} takes values in the finite group μ(ℤ_l).
Uniqueness and the last assertion: ⟨χ_0⟩ maps onto the torsion-free group 1 + qℤ_l, and χ·χ_0^{−k} = ⟨χ_0⟩^{a−k}·(character of finite order).
acceptance: χ = χ_0: a = 1, ε the Teichmüller character ω∘χ_0 of order l − 1 (order 2 for l = 2).
A quadratic character (values ±1 ⊆ ℤ_l^×): a = 0.
Over an imaginary quadratic field F the analogue fails: the anticyclotomic ℤ_l-extension of F gives a character of Gal(F̄/F) that is not of this shape.

sources.excerpt: Aus der Klassenkörpertheorie folgt, daß χ von der Form χ=(l-adische Potenz von χ_0)·(Charakter endlicher Ordnung) ist.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 360. The node makes 'l-adische Potenz' precise through ⟨·⟩ (χ_0^a with a ∈ ℤ_l is not defined on the torsion of ℤ_l^×), and routes the class field theory input to Kronecker-Weber.

nodes.title: The determinant line at the decomposition group of l: L ⊗ C ≅ C(Σ m_i d_i)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the determinant identity, let D ⊆ π̃ = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) be a decomposition group at l, D ≅ Gal(ℚ̄_l/ℚ_l), and C the completion of ℚ̄_l. If (H_i) holds at every place v_i | l, then L ⊗_{ℤ_l} C ≅ C(Σ_{i=1}^r m_i d_i) as semilinear D-modules, where L = Λ^{mh}(Ind_π^π̃ T_l(G)) and m_i = [K_{v_i}:ℚ_l].
hypotheses: π = Gal(K̄/K) ⊆ π̃; the places v_i | l correspond to the double cosets D\π̃/π
(H_i) at every v_i, with d_i as in the Hodge-Tate determinant lemma
proofSteps: Mackey (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1, requested): Res_D Ind_π^π̃ T_l(G) ≅ ⊕_i Ind_{D_i}^D (T_l(G)|_{D_i}), with D_i = D ∩ g_i π g_i^{−1} ≅ Gal(K̄_{v_i}/K_{v_i}) of index m_i in D.
Determinant of an induced representation: det Ind_{D_i}^D U = sgn_{D/D_i}^{dim U}·(det U ∘ Ver_{D→D_i}), with sgn the sign of the permutation action on D/D_i and Ver the transfer.

By the Hodge-Tate determinant lemma, det T_l(G)|_{D_i} = χ_0^{d_i}·η_i with η_i of finite image on the inertia of D_i (R06.2). χ_0|_{D_i} ∘ Ver = χ_0^{m_i}; the transfer maps the inertia of D into the inertia of D_i (inertia is normal in D), so η_i ∘ Ver and sgn have finite image on the inertia of D. Hence the character of D on L is χ_0^{Σ m_i d_i} times a character with finite image on inertia, and L ⊗ C ≅ C(Σ m_i d_i).
acceptance: K = ℚ (m = 1): D_1 = D, no induction, and the lemma is the Hodge-Tate determinant lemma.
l totally split in K (all m_i = 1): L ⊗ C ≅ C(Σ_i d_i), one factor per place.
l inert in K of degree m: one place, m_1 = m, and the twist is m·d_1; the transfer raises χ_0 to the power [D:D_1].

sources.excerpt: Sei C die Komplettierung des algebraischen Abschlusses von ℚ_l, D≅Gal(ℚ̄_l/ℚ_l)⊆π̃ die Zerlegungs-Gruppe von l. Dann gilt als D-Modul L⊗_{ℤ_l}C≅C(+Σ_{i=1}^r m_i d_i) (dies folgt aus unseren vorherigen Berechnungen)
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 360. Faltings says only that this follows from the previous computations; the node spells out the Mackey decomposition and the transfer formula it needs.

nodes.title: Frobenius weights on the induced Tate module: |χ(F_p)| = p^{mh/2} for almost all p
nodes.statement: In the setting of the determinant identity, let p ≠ l be a prime that is unramified in K and such that A has good reduction at every place of K above p (all but finitely many p). Then Ṽ = Ind_π^π̃ V_l(A) is unramified at p, every eigenvalue of an arithmetic Frobenius F_p on Ṽ is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value p^{1/2}, and χ(F_p) = det(F_p | W̃ ⊗ ℚ_l), a product of mh of these eigenvalues, is an algebraic number all of whose conjugates have absolute value p^{mh/2}.
hypotheses: p ≠ l, p unramified in K, A with good reduction at every 𝔭 | p
F_p an arithmetic Frobenius at p in π̃, well defined up to conjugacy and inertia, which acts trivially
proofSteps: At a place 𝔭 ∤ l of good reduction, V_l(A) is unramified and the characteristic polynomial P_𝔭 of Frob_𝔭 has integer coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6, the good-reduction Frobenius polynomial, requested).
Weil's bound (WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.2, requested): the roots of P_𝔭 have all conjugates of absolute value N𝔭^{1/2} = p^{f_𝔭/2}, f_𝔭 the residue degree.

Mackey at p (R01.1): Res_{D_p} Ind_π^π̃ V ≅ ⊕_{𝔭|p} Ind_{D_𝔭}^{D_p} V. As p is unramified in K, inertia acts trivially; F_p permutes the f_𝔭 cosets of D_p/D_𝔭 cyclically with F_p^{f_𝔭} acting as Frob_𝔭, so its characteristic polynomial on Ind_{D_𝔭}^{D_p} V is P_𝔭(T^{f_𝔭}), and its eigenvalues are f_𝔭-th roots of those of Frob_𝔭, with all conjugates of absolute value p^{1/2} ('mit einigen lokalen Überlegungen').
W̃ ⊗ ℚ_l is an F_p-stable subspace of dimension mh, so χ(F_p) is a product of mh eigenvalues of F_p on Ṽ, counted with multiplicity; its conjugates are products of conjugates.
acceptance: m = 1 and G = A[l^∞] (h = 2g): χ(F_p) = det(F_p | V_l(A)) = p^g, of absolute value p^{mh/2}.
Only absolute values are controlled: χ(F_p) need not equal p^{mh/2}; a root of unity may remain.
Excluded primes: p = l, primes ramified in K and primes of bad reduction, finitely many ('für fast alle p').

sources.excerpt: Schließlich folgt aus dem schon von Weil bewiesenen Teil der Weil-Vermutungen mit einigen lokalen Überlegungen, daß χ(F_p) (p=Primzahl, F_p=Frobenius) für fast alle p eine algebraische Zahl ist, all deren Konjugierte Betrag p^{mh/2} haben.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 360; the 'lokale Überlegungen' are the Mackey computation of step 3.

nodes.title: After the shift: #s*(Ω¹_{A_m/A_{m+n}}) = l^{n Σ m_i d_i}
nodes.statement: Let A, l, G, G_n, A_n = A/G_n be as in Satz 2, with v_1, …, v_r the places of K above l and m_i = [K_{v_i}:ℚ_l]. There is m_0 such that for every m ≥ m_0 and every i: (i) the schematic closure in Â_m of the l-divisible group (G/G_m) ∩ H_i^{(m)} over K_i (erratum b)) is an l-divisible group Γ_i over R_i with V_l(Γ_i) = V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i) (erratum a)); (ii) for all n ≥ 0 the finite part of the kernel of A_m → A_{m+n} over R_i is Γ_i[l^n]; hence, with d_i = dim Γ_i, (iii) #(s*(Ω¹_{A_m/A_{m+n}}) ⊗_R R_i) = l^{n m_i d_i} and #s*(Ω¹_{A_m/A_{m+n}}) = l^{n Σ_i m_i d_i}.
hypotheses: the setting of Satz 2; H_i^{(m)} the l-divisible group of Lemma 6 for A_m
the finite part of a quasi-finite flat group scheme over the henselian R_i is its open and closed subgroup finite over R_i
proofSteps: Take m_1 as in erratum b) for all i, then n_0 as in erratum a) for A_{m_1} and the lattices W_i = T_l(G/G_{m_1}) ∩ T_l(Â_{m_1}), and put m_0 = m_1 + n_0; (A_{m_1})_n = A_{m_1+n}. For m ≥ m_0 the closures form l-divisible groups Γ_i over R_i with V_l(Γ_i) = V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i).

Over R_i, the kernel of the extended isogeny A_m → A_{m+n} (Lemma 1) is a quasi-finite flat group scheme. Its finite part (R07.1) has generic fibre the points of (G/G_m)[l^n] that extend into Â_m, i.e. (G/G_m)[l^n] ∩ H_i^{(m)}. Being flat, it is the closure of that generic fibre, i.e. Γ_i[l^n].
The local differential count (R28.2) gives #(s*(Ω¹_{A_m/A_{m+n}}) ⊗ R_i) = #s*(Ω¹_{Γ_i[l^n]/R_i}) = l^{n m_i d_i}.
s*(Ω¹_{A_m/A_{m+n}}) is killed by l^n ('l^n·Ω¹_{A/A_n}=0'), hence supported at the places above l, and its order is the product of the local orders, l^{n Σ_i m_i d_i}.
acceptance: G = A[l^∞] with good reduction at every v_i: Γ_i = A[l^∞] over R_i, d_i = g, and the count l^{n g m} agrees with #s*(Ω¹_{A[l^n]}) from the multiplication-by-l^n check of Lemma 5.
For fixed n the count does not depend on the choice of m ≥ m_0, since d_i is the multiplicity of the weight C_i(1) in (V_l(G) ∩ V_l(H_i)) ⊗ C_i.
Nothing is claimed for m < m_0: for A_0 the kernel's finite part need not be a level of an l-divisible group.

sources.excerpt: Wir übertragen dies nun wieder auf den globalen Fall: Es ist #s*(Ω¹_{A/A_n})=l^{n Σ_{i=1}^r m_i d_i}, (l^n·Ω¹_{A/A_n}=0)
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 359; stated by Faltings for A itself, valid after the shift.

sources.excerpt: Der ursprüngliche Beweis funktioniert jedoch, wenn man gleich zu Beginn A=A_0 durch ein A_m ersetzt, mit genügend großem m.
sources.match: Literal, page image; the shift under which this node holds.

nodes.title: Powers of a principally polarized abelian variety with semiabelian model
nodes.statement: Let A/K be an abelian variety of dimension g with a principal polarization λ and a semiabelian model 𝒜 over R = O_K, and let k ≥ 1. Then A^k carries the product principal polarization λ^k = λ × ⋯ × λ, the fibre power 𝒜^k over R is a semiabelian model of A^k, T_l(A^k) = T_l(A)^k as π-modules, and the alternating form of λ^k on T_l(A^k) is the orthogonal sum of k copies of that of λ. Hence the tower theorem (infinitely many isomorphic quotients) applies to A^k and any π-invariant maximal isotropic subspace of T_l(A)^k ⊗ ℚ_l; Faltings applies it with k = 8.
hypotheses: A/K principally polarized with a semiabelian model over R (after the polarization reduction)
k ≥ 1; A^k the k-fold product (iterated binary product of Tau Ceti)
proofSteps: Products of abelian varieties with projections and the universal property: tauceti AbelianVariety.prod, iterated.
(A^k)^∨ = (A^∨)^k, and λ^k = diag(λ, …, λ) is a polarization of degree (deg λ)^k = 1 (polarizations and duals of products: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3, requested).
The fibre power of a semiabelian scheme is semiabelian: smooth, with fibres connected extensions of B_s^k by T_s^k.
T_l commutes with finite products, and the pairing of a product polarization is the orthogonal sum of the pairings (A3).
acceptance: k = 1 is the tower theorem itself.
k = 8: the form on T_l(A)^8 is the orthogonal sum, which is what makes W_1 = {(x, vx)} ⊕ {(y, −vy)} maximal isotropic when v·ᵗv = −1 (R28.4 quaternion construction).
Degrees: deg(λ^k) = (deg λ)^k, so only principal polarizations stay principal; for λ of degree d > 1 the product has degree d^k.

sources.excerpt: Wenn W ein beliebiger π-invarianter Teilraum von T_l⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l ist, so wendet man obige Überlegungen an auf den maximal isotropen Teilraum W_1={(x,vx)|x∈W^4}⊕{(y,−vy)|y∈(W^⊥)^4}⊆T_l(A)^8⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 361. 'obige Überlegungen' (the tower argument) are applied to A^8 with the product principal polarization; this node records the product facts that application needs, which is the R28.3 target 'companion finiteness statements for products and polarisations'.

nodes.title: Satz 3 and the rational form of Satz 4 are invariant under finite extension and isogeny
nodes.statement: Let A/K be an abelian variety over a number field, l a prime, V = T_l(A) ⊗ ℚ_l, π_K = Gal(K̄/K). (i) If L/K is finite and V is a semisimple π_L-module, then V is a semisimple π_K-module. (ii) If L/K is finite Galois and End_L(A) ⊗ ℚ_l → End_{π_L}(V) is bijective, then End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l → End_{π_K}(V) is bijective. (iii) If A → B is an isogeny over K, then V_l(A) ≅ V_l(B) as π_K-modules and End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ ≅ End_K(B) ⊗ ℚ compatibly with these maps, so the statements of (i) and (ii) hold for A if and only if they hold for B.
hypotheses: K a number field, L/K finite (Galois in (ii)); l a prime
the ℚ_l form of Satz 4, which Faltings says suffices ('Es reicht bekanntlich'), is the one that is invariant; the ℤ_l form is not isogeny invariant
proofSteps: (i) π_L has finite index in π_K. Given a π_K-stable subspace U ⊆ V, choose a π_L-equivariant projection onto U and average it over π_K/π_L (characteristic 0); the result is a π_K-equivariant projection, so U has a π_K-stable complement.

(ii) End_K(A) = End_L(A)^{Gal(L/K)} (Galois descent of homomorphisms: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6, requested) and End_{π_K}(V) = End_{π_L}(V)^{π_K/π_L}; the map is Gal(L/K)-equivariant, and invariants of a bijection are a bijection (invariants commute with ⊗ℚ_l).
(iii) An isogeny f with quasi-inverse g, g∘f = [deg f] (A3), induces V_l(A) ≅ V_l(B) and End⁰(A) ≅ End⁰(B), x ↦ f∘x∘g/deg f, compatibly with the maps to End(V).
acceptance: (i) needs finite index: for the trivial subgroup (infinite index) every V is semisimple.

(ii) needs the invariants: for a CM elliptic curve over ℚ with CM defined over an imaginary quadratic L, End_L(E) ⊗ ℚ is 2-dimensional and End_ℚ(E) ⊗ ℚ = ℚ; both sides shrink by the same Gal(L/ℚ)-invariants.
(iii) is rational only: End(A) ⊗ ℤ_l and End(B) ⊗ ℤ_l can differ for isogenous A, B, which is why Faltings reduces Satz 4 to its ℚ_l form.

sources.locator: §5, p. 360 (start of the proof of Satz 3 and Satz 4)
sources.excerpt: Beweis. Die beiden Sätze werden zusammen bewiesen. Es reicht bekanntlich, statt Satz 4 die etwas schwächere Aussage zu beweisen, daß die Abbildung End_K(A)⊗_ℤℚ_l→End_π(T_l⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l) bijektiv ist.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 360.

sources.excerpt: Man darf dann zum Beweis den Grundkörper erweitern, oder A durch eine isogene abelsche Varietät ersetzen.
sources.match: Literal, page image p. 361; the invariance this node proves.

nodes.title: −1 is a sum of four squares in ℚ_l, for every prime l
nodes.statement: For every prime l there are a, b, c, d ∈ ℤ_l ⊆ ℚ_l with a² + b² + c² + d² = −1.
hypotheses: l any prime, l = 2 included
the source only writes 'Wähle a, b, c, d ∈ ℚ_l mit a² + b² + c² + d² = −1' (p. 361) and does not argue existence
proofSteps: l odd: by ZMod.sq_add_sq choose integers b, c with b² + c² ≡ −2 (mod l) and put d = 0. Then −1 − b² − c² ≡ 1 (mod l), so F(X) = X² + 1 + b² + c² satisfies ‖F(1)‖ < 1 = ‖F′(1)‖² (F′(1) = 2 is an l-adic unit), and Hensel's lemma gives a ∈ ℤ_l with a² = −1 − b² − c².
l = 2: take b = c = 1, d = 2 and F(X) = X² + 7. Then ‖F(1)‖ = ‖8‖ = 1/8 < 1/4 = ‖F′(1)‖², and Hensel's lemma gives a ∈ ℤ_2 with a² = −7; then a² + 1 + 1 + 4 = −1.
acceptance: The case l = 2 is covered by an explicit quadruple, not excluded.
At l = 3: b = 1, c = 0 gives b² + c² = 1 ≡ −2 (mod 3), and a² = −2 has a 3-adic solution with a ≡ ±1 (mod 3).
The solution is integral, so the construction works over ℤ_l too, although the source needs only ℚ_l.

sources.excerpt: Wähle a, b, c, d∈ℚ_l mit a²+b²+c²+d²=−1.
sources.match: The source takes the existence of such a quadruple for granted; this node proves it, for l = 2 with the explicit quadruple (a, 1, 1, 2), a² = −7.

nodes.title: Zarhin's lemma: a π-invariant maximal isotropic W ⊆ V_l(A) is the image of an idempotent of End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with ring of integers R, A/K a principally polarized abelian variety extending to a semiabelian variety over Spec(R), l a prime, W ⊆ V_l(A) = T_l(A) ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l a π-invariant maximal isotropic subspace for the Weil pairing, G ⊆ A[l^∞] the corresponding l-divisible group and A_n = A/G_n. Then there is u ∈ End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l with u(V_l(A)) = W, and consequently an idempotent e ∈ End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l with e(V_l(A)) = W.
hypotheses: the hypotheses of the node infinitely-many-isomorphic-quotients-along-a-maximal-isotropic-tower, whose conclusion (infinitely many A_n are K-isomorphic) is the only input from heights
T_l(A_n) ≅ X_n := (T_l(A) ∩ W) + l^n·T_l(A) as π-modules, through the isogeny A_n → A induced by multiplication by l^n, which kills G_n ⊆ A[l^n]

End_K(A) is a free ℤ-module of finite rank, End_K(A) ⊗ ℤ_l → End(T_l(A)) is injective, and End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ is semisimple (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6); hence End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l is semisimple (characteristic 0)
Faltings writes only 'Wie in [16] folgt daraus'; the argument used is the one written out in Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Lemma 2.4
proofSteps: Put T = T_l(A), V = V_l(A), X_n = (T ∩ W) + l^n·T. The isogeny f_n : A_n → A induced by multiplication by l^n maps T_l(A_n) isomorphically onto X_n (R01.6, compatibility of T_l with isogenies).
By the preceding node there is an infinite set I of indices such that all A_i, i ∈ I, are K-isomorphic; let i_0 = min I and fix isomorphisms v_i : A_{i_0} → A_i.
u_i = f_i ∘ v_i ∘ f_{i_0}^{−1} lies in End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ ⊆ End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l and maps X_{i_0} onto X_i ⊆ X_{i_0}; so every u_i lies in the compact set End_{ℤ_l}(X_{i_0}) (ℤ_l is compact).
Pass to a convergent subsequence u_i → u. End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l is a finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace of End(V), so u ∈ End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l.
u(X_{i_0}) ⊆ ⋂_i X_i = T ∩ W. Conversely each y ∈ ⋂_i X_i is u_i(x_i) with x_i ∈ X_{i_0}; a limit point x of (x_i) satisfies u(x) = y. So u(X_{i_0}) = T ∩ W and u(V) = W.

a = {w ∈ End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l : w(V) ⊆ W} is a right ideal of the semisimple algebra End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l, hence a = e·(End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l) for an idempotent e (IsSemisimpleRing.ideal_eq_span_idempotent in the opposite ring); u ∈ a gives W = u(V) ⊆ e(V) ⊆ W.
acceptance: The limit u is shown to lie in End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l (closedness of a finite-dimensional subspace), not merely in End_π(V).
Surjectivity u(V) = W is proved by the second compactness argument, not only u(V) ⊆ W.
Only infinitely many isomorphic members of the tower are used, which is what the corrected Satz 2 and Satz 1 give; no equality h(A_n) = h(A) for all n is needed.

sources.excerpt: Nach Satz 2 ist h(A_n)=h(A), und nach Satz 1 sind unendlich viele A_n's isomorph. Wie in [16] folgt daraus, daß W Bild eines Idempotents aus End_K(A)⊗_ℤℚ_l ist.
sources.match: The statement of the lemma; its proof is cited to Zarhin [16] and not printed. 'h(A_n) = h(A)' is corrected in the Zusatz bei der Korrektur (p. 366) to eventual stationarity, which is all the lemma needs.

sources.locator: Chapter IV, §2, Lemma 2.4 and its proof, printed pp. 136–137
sources.excerpt: LEMMA 2.4. Suppose A satisfies (*). For any W ⊂ V_ℓA stable under Γ, there is a u ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q_ℓ such that uV_ℓA = W.
sources.match: Milne proves this under (*) (finitely many B ℓ-power isogenous to A); the proof uses only an infinite set of pairwise isomorphic members of the tower X_n = (T_ℓ ∩ W) + ℓ^n T_ℓ, which the preceding node supplies for maximal isotropic W.

nodes.title: Every π-invariant subspace of V_l(A) is the image of an idempotent of End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l (quaternion transfer)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A/K a principally polarized abelian variety extending to a semiabelian variety over Spec(R), and l a prime. Then every π-invariant ℚ_l-subspace W of V_l(A) is e(V_l(A)) for an idempotent e ∈ End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l. The same holds for A × A.
hypotheses: A^8 with the product principal polarization is principally polarized and extends to the eighth power of the semiabelian model; V_l(A^8) = V_l(A)^8 with the orthogonal-sum Weil pairing, and End_K(A^8) ⊗ ℚ_l = M_8(End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l) acting by matrices
E = End_K(A) ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l is semisimple (A6)
A × A is principally polarized with a semiabelian model as well, so the statement applies to it (the graph argument for Satz 4 needs it)
proofSteps: Choose a, b, c, d ∈ ℚ_l with a² + b² + c² + d² = −1 (node minus-one-is-a-sum-of-four-squares-in-Q_l) and form W_1 ⊆ V_l(A^8) (quaternion construction); W_1 is π-invariant and maximal isotropic.
Zarhin's lemma for A^8 and W_1 gives an idempotent e_1 ∈ M_8(E) with e_1(V^8) = W_1.

Let p : V^8 → V^4, (s, t) ↦ ½(s + v⁻¹t), and pr_1 : V^4 → V the first coordinate; both are matrices with entries in ℚ_l ⊆ E. Since p(W_1) = W^4, W = pr_1(p(e_1(V^8))) = w_1(V) + … + w_8(V), where (w_1, …, w_8) = pr_1·p·e_1 has entries w_j ∈ E.
a = {w ∈ E : w(V) ⊆ W} is a right ideal of the semisimple E containing every w_j, so a = eE for an idempotent e, and W = Σ w_j(V) ⊆ e(V) ⊆ W.
A × A satisfies the same hypotheses, so the same argument gives the statement for A × A.
acceptance: The transport from A^8 back to A (recovery map and right ideal) is written out, not left as 'der Rest des Beweises'.
The idempotent lies in End_K(A) ⊗ ℚ_l for the field K over which A is principally polarized and semiabelian (possibly enlarged by the reduction node).
A line W in V_l of an elliptic curve (so W^⊥ = W, isotropic but maximal only in dimension 2) is covered: W_1 = W^4 × W^4.

sources.excerpt: Der Rest des Beweises geht genauso wie in [16], und sei daher nur skizziert: … Wenn W ein beliebiger π-invarianter Teilraum von T_l⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l ist, so wendet man obige Überlegungen an auf den maximal isotropen Teilraum W_1
sources.match: The source applies the maximal isotropic case to W_1 and leaves the passage back to W unprinted; this node supplies it.

sources.locator: Chapter IV, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5(a), printed p. 138
sources.excerpt: This is a right ideal in End(A)⊗Q_ℓ, and aV_ℓA = W because the hypothesis on A and (2.4) imply there exists a u ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q_ℓ such that uV_ℓA = W. From the above remarks, we know that a is generated by an idempotent e
sources.match: The right-ideal step used in the last two proof steps.

nodes.title: Korollar 2 to Satz 4: the isogeny criterion by rational Tate modules and local L-factors
nodes.statement: Let A_1, A_2 be abelian varieties over the number field K and l a prime. For the almost all places v of K at which A_1 and A_2 have good reduction and v ∤ l, let L_v(A_i, s) = det(1 − (Nv)^{−s}·F_v | T_l(A_i))^{−1}, which is independent of l. The following are equivalent: (i) A_1 and A_2 are isogenous over K; (ii) T_l(A_1) ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l ≅ T_l(A_2) ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l as π-modules; (iii) L_v(s, A_1) = L_v(s, A_2) for almost all places v of K; (iv) L_v(s, A_1) = L_v(s, A_2) for all v, where at the remaining finitely many places L_v is defined with the inertia invariants of T_{l'} for a prime l' different from the residue characteristic.
hypotheses: A_1, A_2 abelian varieties over the number field K; (i) means isogenous over K
(ii) is printed with ⊗_ℤ ℚ_l; ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l is meant (source issue)
the printed definition of L_v covers only almost all v; (iv) uses the standard definition at the remaining places (source issue)
(ii) ⇔ (iii) uses Satz 3, the Chebotarev density theorem and the trace criterion for semisimple representations in characteristic 0
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii): an isogeny φ : A_1 → A_2 induces T_l(φ) injective with finite cokernel (R01.6), hence an isomorphism after ⊗ ℚ_l.

(ii) ⇒ (i): by Korollar 1, Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗ ℚ_l → Hom_π(V_l(A_1), V_l(A_2)) is bijective, and dim V_l(A_1) = dim V_l(A_2) forces dim A_1 = dim A_2. After fixing bases, det V_l(f) is a polynomial function on Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗ ℚ_l that is nonzero at the given isomorphism, so it is nonzero at some f in the dense subgroup Hom_K(A_1, A_2) ⊗ ℚ; an integer multiple n·f is a homomorphism with V_l(n·f) an isomorphism, so its kernel is finite and it is an isogeny (A6, R01.6).
(ii) ⇒ (iii): isomorphic V_l have equal characteristic polynomials of F_v at every place of good reduction not above l, and L_v is independent of l (R01.6).

(iii) ⇒ (ii): V_l(A_1) ⊕ V_l(A_2) is unramified outside the places of bad reduction and the places above l (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, R11.5). By Chebotarev (every Frobenius class of a finite Galois extension occurs at infinitely many places) every element of the image of π is a limit of Frobenius elements at places where (iii) holds, so tr(σ | V_l(A_1)) = tr(σ | V_l(A_2)) for all σ ∈ π by continuity. Both are semisimple (Satz 3), hence isomorphic by the trace criterion (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1/trace-determines-semisimple).

(iv) ⇒ (iii) is trivial. (i) ⇒ (iv): an isogeny gives V_{l'}(A_1) ≅ V_{l'}(A_2) for every l', hence equal inertia invariants and equal local factors at every place. So the printed 'aus ii) folgt iv)' goes through (i).
acceptance: (iii) concerns almost all v: a finite set of places cannot separate isogeny classes.
Without Satz 3, equal Frobenius traces give only equal semisimplifications; semisimplicity is used in (iii) ⇒ (ii).

The curves 11a1, 11a2, 11a3 over ℚ are isogenous and have equal a_p (a_2 = −2, a_3 = −1, a_5 = 1, a_7 = −2); 37a1 and 37b1 share a_7 = −1 but have a_2 = −2 and 0, so agreement at finitely many primes does not give (iii).

sources.excerpt: Korollar 2. Seien A_1, A_2 wie im Korollar 1. Es sind äquivalent i) A_1 und A_2 sind isogen. ii) T_l(A_1)⊗_ℤℚ_l≅T_l(A_2)⊗_ℤℚ_l als π-Modul. iii) L_v(s, A_1)=L_v(s, A_2) für fast alle Stellen v von K. iv) L_v(s, A_1)=L_v(s, A_2) für alle v.
sources.match: Literal statement as printed (including the misprinted ⊗_ℤ in ii), recorded as a source issue).

sources.locator: Section 5, definition of L(A, s) and proof of Korollar 2, p. 361
sources.excerpt: wobei das Produkt über fast alle Stellen von K zu erstrecken ist. Die lokalen L-Faktoren L_v(A, s) sind unabhängig von l. … Die Äquivalenz von i) und ii) folgt aus Satz 4, die von ii) und iii) aus Satz 3 (+Čebotarev), und aus ii) folgt iv) folgt iii) ist trivial.
sources.match: The definition of L_v at almost all places and the one-line proof.

sources.excerpt: LEMMA 3.9. Let k be a field of characteristic zero, and let R be a k-algebra of finite dimension over k. Two semisimple R-modules of finite-dimension over k are isomorphic if they have the same trace.
sources.match: The trace criterion used in (iii) ⇒ (ii).

nodes.title: The twisted determinant character χ·ε^h is unramified outside l
nodes.statement: Let B_1/K be an abelian variety with semistable reduction everywhere, l a prime, G ⊆ B_1[l] a π-stable subgroup of order l^h, W_l = G(K̄) ⊆ V_l = B_1[l](K̄), W̃_l = Ind_π^{π̃}(W_l) (an 𝔽_l-space of dimension mh, m = [K:ℚ]), and χ : π̃ → (ℤ/lℤ)^* the character of π̃ on the line Λ^{mh}(W̃_l). Let ε : π̃ → {±1} be the character of π̃ on Λ^m Ind_π^{π̃}(ℤ), the sign of the permutation action on π̃/π. Then χ·ε^h is unramified at every prime p' ≠ l.
hypotheses: semistable reduction of B_1 at the places v ∤ l, used only through the unipotence of the inertia groups I_v on V_l (Grothendieck's monodromy criterion, R11.3)
the source gives the reason in one clause: 'denn die Trägheitsgruppen der Stellen v von K, welche l nicht teilen, operieren unipotent auf V_l (semistabile Reduktion)'
proofSteps: Determinant of an induced representation: for σ ∈ π̃, split π̃/π into ⟨σ⟩-orbits. On the block of Ind(W_l) belonging to an orbit of length f with representative t, σ acts by a block-cyclic matrix of determinant sgn(f-cycle)^{dim W_l}·det(t⁻¹σ^f t | W_l), with t⁻¹σ^f t ∈ π. Over all orbits, χ(σ) = ε(σ)^h·∏ det(t⁻¹σ^f t | W_l) = ε(σ)^h·det(W_l)(Ver(σ)), Ver the transfer π̃ → π^{ab} (Mathlib's explicit formula for the transfer).
Hence χ·ε^h = det(W_l) ∘ Ver, since ε² = 1.

For σ in an inertia group I_{p'} at p' ≠ l, each t⁻¹σ^f t lies in π ∩ t⁻¹I_{p'}t, an inertia group of a place of K above p', which acts unipotently on V_l and hence on the stable subspace W_l; its determinant is 1.
So χ·ε^h is trivial on every inertia group at every p' ≠ l.
acceptance: Without the twist the character can be ramified where K/ℚ ramifies: ε is the sign of the permutation representation on π̃/π; for K = ℚ(√D), ε is the quadratic character of K/ℚ.
Only unipotence (semistability) at v ∤ l is used, not good reduction.
For K = ℚ (m = 1), ε is trivial and χ = det(W_l).

sources.excerpt: Wenn ε: π̃→{±1} den Charakter bezeichnet, mit dem π̃ auf Λ^m Ind_π^{π̃}(ℤ) operiert, so ist χ·ε^h unverzweigt außerhalb l, denn die Trägheitsgruppen der Stellen v von K, welche l nicht teilen, operieren unipotent auf V_l (semistabile Reduktion).
sources.match: Literal; the determinant-of-induction computation that turns unipotence at places of K into unramifiedness at primes of ℚ is left implicit and is written out here.

nodes.title: A mod-l character of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) unramified outside l is a power of the cyclotomic character
nodes.statement: Let l be a prime and ψ : Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) → (ℤ/lℤ)^* a continuous character unramified at every prime p' ≠ l. Then ψ = χ_0^k for some integer k, where χ_0 is the mod-l cyclotomic character (σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ_0(σ)} for every l-th root of unity ζ).
hypotheses: this is the source's 'Nach der Klassenkörpertheorie ist χ·ε^h eine Potenz des zyklotomischen Charakters χ_0'
ψ takes values in 𝔽_l^*, a group of order prime to l
proofSteps: The fixed field F of ker ψ is a finite abelian extension of ℚ unramified outside l (no condition at the archimedean place).
Kronecker–Weber (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory, Layer 13) gives F ⊆ ℚ(ζ_n) for some n; write n = l^a·n' with l ∤ n'.

Gal(ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/l^a)^* × (ℤ/n')^* (Mathlib's galEquivZMod), and the inertia groups at the primes dividing n' generate the factor (ℤ/n')^* (ramification in cyclotomic fields, GlobalNumberFields Layer 10). F is unramified at those primes, so F ⊆ ℚ(ζ_{l^a}).

ψ factors through (ℤ/l^a)^*; the kernel of (ℤ/l^a)^* → (ℤ/l)^* is an l-group and ψ has order prime to l, so ψ factors through (ℤ/l)^* = Gal(ℚ(ζ_l)/ℚ), which is cyclic and generated by χ_0; hence ψ = χ_0^k.
acceptance: At l = 2 the target 𝔽_2^* is trivial and the statement is vacuous.
For l ≡ 3 mod 4 the quadratic character of ℚ(√−l)/ℚ is unramified outside l and equals χ_0^{(l−1)/2}.
Ramification at the archimedean place is allowed: χ_0 itself is odd.

sources.excerpt: Nach der Klassenkörpertheorie ist χ·ε^h eine Potenz des zyklotomischen Charakters χ_0.
sources.match: Literal; the class field theory used is Kronecker–Weber together with the ramification of cyclotomic fields.

nodes.title: Heights agree along isogenies of l-power degree with l > N
nodes.statement: Let A/K have semistable reduction everywhere, let N be as in the node on the choice of N, and let φ : B_1 → B_2 be an isogeny between abelian varieties over K isogenous to A whose degree is a power of a prime l > N. Then h(B_1) = h(B_2).
hypotheses: B_1, B_2 isogenous to A, hence semistable everywhere and with good reduction at the places above l
l > N ≥ np, so l ∤ pn
proofSteps: Factor φ into isogenies whose kernels are killed by l (filter ker φ by its l-torsion); every intermediate variety is isogenous to A. So one may assume l·ker φ = 0 ('Wir dürfen annehmen, daß l den Kern G von φ annulliert').
Let deg φ = l^h. By the Raynaud node, χ·ε^h = χ_0^d with l^d = #s^*(Ω^1_{G/R}) and 0 ≦ d ≦ gm.

χ(F_p) is the eigenvalue of F_p on the line L ⊆ Λ^{mh}(Ṽ_l), so it is a root modulo l of the characteristic polynomial of F_p on Λ^{mh}(Ind_π^{π̃}(T_l(B_1))), which is P_{mh}(T) because V_l(B_1) ≅ V_l(A). As χ(F_p) = ε(F_p)^h·χ_0(F_p)^d = ±p^d, l divides P_{mh}(±p^d). (The printed 'χ_0^d(F_p) = ±p^d' should read χ(F_p) = ±p^d; source issue.)
Since 0 ≦ mh ≦ 2gm, 0 ≦ d ≦ gm and l > N, the choice of N forces d = mh/2.
Lemma 5: h(B_2) − h(B_1) = ½·log(l^h) − (1/m)·log(l^d) = log(l)·(h/2 − d/m) = 0.
acceptance: Only isogenies of l-power degree with l > N are covered; the finitely many l ≦ N are handled by the lattice argument.
F_p is the Frobenius at the fixed auxiliary prime p ∤ n, and p ≠ l because l > N ≥ np.
The reduction to kernels killed by l keeps every intermediate variety in the isogeny class of A, so the Raynaud node applies at every step.

sources.excerpt: Wir werden zeigen, daß für jede Isogenie φ: B_1→B_2 von zu A isogenen abelschen Varietäten, deren Grad eine l-Potenz mit einer Primzahl l>N ist, h(B_1) und h(B_2) übereinstimmen. … Wir dürfen annehmen, daß l den Kern G von φ annulliert.
sources.match: Literal statement of the claim and the first reduction.

sources.excerpt: Also ist χ_0^d(F_p)=±p^d eine Nullstelle von P_{mh}(T) modulo l, und nach Wahl von N muß d=hm/2 gelten. Da wieder h(B_2)−h(B_1)=log(l)(h/2−d/m), folgt unsere Behauptung
sources.match: Literal conclusion (with the misprint χ_0^d(F_p) for χ(F_p)).

sources.locator: Appendix to Chapter IV (Milne's review of Faltings 1983), printed p. 159
sources.excerpt: THEOREM (*) Let A be an abelian variety over K with semistable reduction everywhere; then there is an N such that for every isogeny A → B of degree prime to N, h(A) = h(B).
sources.match: The same statement as it is usually quoted.

nodes.title: For each prime l, the l-part of exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) takes finitely many values on the isogeny class
nodes.statement: Let A/K have semistable reduction everywhere and fix a prime l. As B ranges over the abelian varieties over K isogenous to A, the exponent of l in the rational number exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) takes only finitely many values.
hypotheses: all B isogenous to A are semistable everywhere, so their heights are defined through their semiabelian models
the rationality of exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B) − h(A))) is the Bemerkung after Lemma 5
proofSteps: For B isogenous to A choose an isogeny ψ : B → A; T_l(ψ) identifies T_l(B) with a π-stable lattice Λ_B in V_l(A) (R01.6).

If Λ_{B_1} ≅ Λ_{B_2}, i.e. T_l(B_1) ≅ T_l(B_2) as π-modules, then Korollar 1 and l-adic approximation give an isogeny B_1 → B_2 of degree prime to l, and the Bemerkung after Lemma 5 shows that l does not occur in exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B_1) − h(B_2))).
So the l-exponent depends only on the isomorphism class of Λ_B, and the lattice node (with Satz 3) gives finitely many classes.
acceptance: The bound is per prime l; Satz 6 uses it for the finitely many l ≦ N only.
The input from Satz 4 is an isogeny of degree prime to l between B_1 and B_2, which needs Korollar 1 (Satz 4 for B_1 × B_2), although the source says 'nach Satz 4'.
Varieties with isomorphic T_l can have different heights; only the l-part of the difference is controlled.

sources.excerpt: Wenn für zwei abelsche Varietäten B_1/K und B_2/K T_l(B_1) und T_l(B_2) als π-Moduln isomorph sind, so existiert nach Satz 4 eine Isogenie vom Grad prim zu l zwischen B_1 und B_2, und l tritt nicht in exp(2[K:ℚ](h(B_1)−h(B_2))) auf.
sources.match: Literal; the reduction of the small-prime bound to the lattice finiteness.

nodes.title: Shafarevich finiteness without polarization (Finiteness II)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places of K and g ≥ 1. Then there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of abelian varieties over K of dimension g with good reduction outside S.
hypotheses: no polarization is fixed, as the R28.5 stage text demands ('finiteness of abelian varieties of fixed dimension over F with good reduction outside a fixed finite set'); Faltings' Satz 6 is stated for d-fold polarized varieties

the transfer uses Zarhin's trick and the finiteness of direct factors, which the R28.1 stage text assigns to R28.1 ('Use Zarhin's trick or the appropriate polarisation argument to remove unnecessary polarisation restrictions, with a proof of the resulting finiteness transfer'); no R28.1 node states them yet (gap)
proofSteps: For A of dimension g with good reduction outside S, A^∨ has good reduction outside S (dual abelian scheme, A6), and C = (A × A^∨)^4 is principally polarized (Zarhin's trick, Milne I Theorem 13.12), of dimension 8g, with good reduction outside S.
Satz 6 with d = 1 and dimension 8g gives finitely many such C up to K-isomorphism.

A is a direct factor of C, and an abelian variety has only finitely many direct factors up to isomorphism (Milne I Theorem 15.3); hence finitely many A. This is the argument of Milne I Corollary 13.13 over a number field.
acceptance: No bound on a polarization degree is assumed; a polarization of unbounded degree would not reduce to Satz 6 directly.
For g = 1 the statement is Satz 6 with d = 1 (elliptic curves are canonically principally polarized), Shafarevich's theorem.
Only finiteness of isomorphism classes of the varieties is claimed; each has finitely many polarizations of a given degree (Milne I Theorem 15.1), which is the converse transfer.

sources.excerpt: THEOREM 1.4 (FINITENESS II). Given a number field k, an integer g, and a finite set of finite primes S of k, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of abelian varieties A over k of dimension g having good reduction outside S.
sources.match: The unpolarized statement the stage text asks for.

sources.locator: Chapter I, §13, Corollary 13.13 and its proof, printed p. 61
sources.excerpt: From (13.12) we know that (A × A^∨)^4 has a principal polarization, and according to (11.2), the abelian varieties of dimension 8g over k having principal polarizations fall into finitely many isomorphism classes. But A is a direct factor of (A × A^∨)^4
sources.match: The transfer argument (over a finite field there; here with Satz 6 in place of (11.2)).

nodes.title: Semisimplicity of V_l(E) for an elliptic curve over a number field
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, E/K an elliptic curve (a Weierstrass curve over K with nonzero discriminant) and l a prime. Then V_l(E) = T_l(E) ⊗_{ℤ_l} ℚ_l is a semisimple ℚ_l[Gal(K̄/K)]-module: it is irreducible or the direct sum of two Galois-stable lines.
hypotheses: T_l(E) is the Tate module of the Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves, Layer 2)
E is regarded as a one-dimensional abelian variety A_E over K with T_l(E) ≅ T_l(A_E) as Galois modules; this identification is in neither library (gap)
proofSteps: Transport Satz 3 for A_E along T_l(E) ≅ T_l(A_E).
A semisimple two-dimensional representation is irreducible or a sum of two stable lines.
acceptance: For E without complex multiplication over ℚ, V_l(E) is irreducible for every l even when E[l] is reducible (e.g. l = 5 for 11a1): a stable line in V_l(E) would give infinitely many cyclic isogenies of l-power degree, contradicting the finiteness of the isogeny class.
For y² = x³ − x over K = ℚ(i), V_l(E) is a sum of two characters.
The statement is about V_l(E), not E[l]: E[l] may be reducible and non-semisimple.

sources.excerpt: Satz 3. Die Operation von π auf T_l⊗_{ℤ_l}ℚ_l ist halbeinfach.
sources.match: Satz 3 for g = 1.

sources.excerpt: THEOREM 1.2 (SEMISIMPLICITY). Let A be an abelian variety over a number field k; for all primes ℓ, the action of Gal(k^al/k) on V_ℓA is semisimple.
sources.match: The statement exported by R28.6 for the elliptic-curve type.

nodes.title: Hom_K(E, E') ⊗ ℤ_l ≅ Hom_{G_K}(T_l E, T_l E') for elliptic curves
nodes.statement: For elliptic curves E, E' over a number field K and a prime l, the natural map Hom_K(E, E') ⊗_ℤ ℤ_l → Hom_{Gal(K̄/K)}(T_l(E), T_l(E')) is an isomorphism, where Hom_K(E, E') is Tau Ceti's group of homomorphisms of Weierstrass curves (the zero map and the isogenies defined over K). Consequently Hom_K(E, E') ⊗ ℚ_l ≅ Hom_{Gal(K̄/K)}(V_l(E), V_l(E')).
hypotheses: the Tate modules and the action of an isogeny on them come from Tau Ceti EllipticCurves, Layer 2
Hom_K(E, E') ≅ Hom_K(A_E, A_E') as groups and T_l(E) ≅ T_l(A_E) equivariantly, for the associated one-dimensional abelian varieties (gap)
proofSteps: Transport Korollar 1 along the identification of E with A_E.
Injectivity and surjectivity both come from Korollar 1; the map sends an isogeny to its action on Tate modules.
acceptance: For E = E' over ℚ, End_ℚ(E) = ℤ, so End_{G_ℚ}(T_l(E)) = ℤ_l, curves with complex multiplication included.
For 11a1 and 11a3 over ℚ (linked by a 5-isogeny) both sides are free of rank one over ℤ_l.
For 37a1 and 37b1 over ℚ both sides vanish.

sources.excerpt: Korollar 1. Seien A_1 und A_2 abelsche Varietäten über K. Dann ist Hom_K(A_1, A_2)⊗_ℤℤ_l→Hom_π(T_l(A_1), T_l(A_2)) ein Isomorphismus.
sources.match: Korollar 1 for g = 1.

nodes.title: The isogeny criterion for elliptic curves
nodes.statement: Elliptic curves E, E' over a number field K are K-isogenous if and only if V_l(E) ≅ V_l(E') as Gal(K̄/K)-modules for one (equivalently every) prime l, if and only if a_v(E) = a_v(E') for almost all places v at which both have good reduction.
hypotheses: for elliptic curves with good reduction at v, L_v(E, s)^{−1} = 1 − a_v·Nv^{−s} + Nv^{1−2s}, so equality of local factors is equality of a_v
the identification of E with a one-dimensional abelian variety is a gap, as for the other nodes of this layer
proofSteps: Transport Korollar 2 along the identification of E with A_E.
Condition (iii) of Korollar 2 becomes a_v(E) = a_v(E') for almost all v.
acceptance: 11a1, 11a2 and 11a3 are isogenous over ℚ and have a_2 = −2, a_3 = −1, a_5 = 1, a_7 = −2.
37a1 and 37b1 share a_7 = −1 but have a_2 = −2 and 0, so they are not isogenous: agreement at finitely many primes is not enough.
A quadratic twist E^D of E (D not a square, E without complex multiplication) is not isogenous to E, and a_p(E^D) = −a_p(E) at the primes p inert in ℚ(√D).

sources.excerpt: Korollar 2. Seien A_1, A_2 wie im Korollar 1. Es sind äquivalent i) A_1 und A_2 sind isogen. ii) T_l(A_1)⊗_ℤℚ_l≅T_l(A_2)⊗_ℤℚ_l als π-Modul. iii) L_v(s, A_1)=L_v(s, A_2) für fast alle Stellen v von K.
sources.match: Korollar 2 for g = 1 (⊗_ℤ is a misprint for ⊗_{ℤ_l}).

nodes.title: Finiteness of the K-isogeny class of an elliptic curve
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K. Up to K-isomorphism there are only finitely many elliptic curves E'/K that are K-isogenous to E.
hypotheses: an elliptic curve carries a canonical principal polarization, and a K-isomorphism of elliptic curves respects it
a curve K-isogenous to E has good reduction outside the set S of places of bad reduction of E (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich for elliptic curves, Tau Ceti EllipticCurves, Layer 4)
the identification of elliptic curves with principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension one is a gap, as for the other nodes of this layer
proofSteps: Let S be the places of bad reduction of E. If E' is K-isogenous to E, then V_l(E') ≅ V_l(E) for all l, so E' has good reduction outside S.

As principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension one, the E' are 1-fold polarized with good reduction outside S, so Satz 6 (g = 1, d = 1) gives finitely many K-isomorphism classes; these are the K-isomorphism classes of the elliptic curves.
acceptance: For E = 11a1 over ℚ the ℚ-isogeny class consists of exactly three ℚ-isomorphism classes, 11a1, 11a2 and 11a3.
The count is of K-isomorphism classes: quadratic twists of E are in general not K-isogenous to E and are not counted.
Consequence used by EllipticCurveModularity R29.1: together with the rank-one node, E/ℚ has rational cyclic isogenies of only finitely many prime degrees.

sources.excerpt: Satz 6 (Shafarevich-Vermutung). Sei S eine endliche Menge von Stellen von K, d>0. Dann gibt es nur endlich viele Isomorphie-Klassen d-fach polarisierter abelscher Varietäten über K von vorgegebener Dimension, welche außerhalb S gute Reduktion haben.
sources.match: Satz 6 with g = 1 and d = 1.

sources.excerpt: THEOREM 1.1 (FINITENESS I). Let A be an abelian variety over an algebraic number field k. Then, up to isomorphism, there are only finitely many abelian varieties B over k that are isogenous to A.
sources.match: The general statement, of which this node is the elliptic-curve case that the R28.6 stage text asks for.

nodes.title: Hom_K(E, E') is infinite cyclic when E' is isogenous to E and End_K(E') = ℤ
nodes.statement: Let E, E' be elliptic curves over a field K with Hom_K(E, E') ≠ 0 and End_K(E') = ℤ (every K-endomorphism of E' is multiplication by an integer). Then Hom_K(E, E') is infinite cyclic; if f_0 generates it, every nonzero f ∈ Hom_K(E, E') is n·f_0 with n ≠ 0, and deg f = n²·deg f_0.
hypotheses: no finiteness or number-field hypothesis is needed
over K = ℚ, End_ℚ(E') = ℤ for every elliptic curve E' (EllipticCurveModularity R29.1), curves with complex multiplication included
the dual isogeny supplies a nonzero ψ ∈ Hom_K(E', E) (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves, Layer 1)
proofSteps: Fix a nonzero ψ ∈ Hom_K(E', E), the dual of a nonzero element of Hom_K(E, E').
f ↦ f ∘ ψ is an additive map Hom_K(E, E') → End_K(E') (Tau Ceti Hom.add_comp) and is injective (Hom.comp_eq_zero_iff: f ∘ ψ = 0 forces f = 0).
Its image is a nonzero subgroup of End_K(E') = ℤ, hence infinite cyclic, and so is Hom_K(E, E').
deg(n·f_0) = n²·deg f_0 (Tau Ceti Hom.degree_zsmul).
acceptance: For E = E' = 11a1 over ℚ, Hom = ℤ generated by the identity, and deg[n] = n².
For 11a1 and 11a2 over ℚ the nonzero homomorphisms have degrees 5·n²: a generator is a 5-isogeny.
The hypothesis End_K(E') = ℤ is necessary: over K = ℚ(i), y² = x³ − x has End_K = ℤ[i], of rank two.

sources.excerpt: THEOREM 10.15. For any abelian varieties A and B, and ℓ ≠ char(k), the natural map Hom(A, B) ⊗ Z_ℓ → Hom(T_ℓA, T_ℓB) is injective, with torsion-free cokernel. Hence Hom(A, B) is a free Z-module of finite rank ≤ 4 dim(A) dim(B).
sources.match: The general finite generation; the sharper rank-one statement for End_K(E') = ℤ, which the R28.6 stage text asks for ('the finite-generation and rank-one Hom consequence when End_Q(E)=Z'), follows by the elementary argument of the proof steps.

coverage.note: Sections 2 and 3 of Faltings' paper, decomposed to declaration granularity: semiabelian schemes with the Hodge line bundle and its four properties, the unique extension of a homomorphism over a dense open of a normal base, the proper correspondence stack over the integers carrying a stable curve and the two homomorphisms to the universal abelian variety, the two-sided comparison of the modular and the Hodge bundle with a constant depending only on the dimension, metrized line bundles with their arithmetic degree and the modular height, the logarithmic singularities of the Hodge metric along the degeneration locus, the Northcott statement for heights from such metrics, and Satz 1. The reviewed library audit records the layer as not built: neither pinned library has a polarisation, a moduli space, an arithmetic degree or a height of an abelian variety, so every node here is genuinely new.

Section 4: Lemma 5, the isogeny height formula, with the remark bounding the denominators of the height difference by primes dividing the isogeny degree; Lemma 6, the triviality of the inertia action on the quotient of the Tate module by the Tate module of the toric part, whose orthogonality input the reviewer located in SGA 7 I, Expose IX 7.4.3; the local differential computations Faltings imports from Tate; and the global determinant identity that forces the sum of the local multiplicities to be half the height. The audit records the layer as not built, with no Faltings height and no p-divisible group in either library.

The 1984 erratum and the corrected form of Satz 2. Both corrections are separate nodes: the Zariski closures of the kernels form an l-divisible group only after passing to a member of the tower with large index, and the intersection with the toric l-divisible group is l-divisible only after the same shift. Satz 2 is recorded only in its corrected form, that the sequence of heights becomes stationary after replacing the variety by a member of the tower, and the consequence that infinitely many members are isomorphic is a separate node, as is the polarisation and semistability reduction at the start of the proof of Satz 3 and Satz 4. The reviewer of the integrated decomposition re-parented that reduction here to remove a stage cycle, and this packet keeps that parenting.

Section 5: the quaternion construction of a Galois-invariant maximal isotropic subspace, with the coefficients in the l-adic rationals as the reviewer corrected; Satz 3 and Satz 4, the semisimplicity of the rational Tate module and the comparison of the rational homomorphism group with the module of Galois-equivariant maps; the pair form of the comparison with the isogeny criterion; and the finiteness of polarized varieties with all Tate modules isomorphic. The audit records that neither library has a Tate module of an abelian variety at all.

Section 6: Satz 5, the finiteness of the isogeny classes with good reduction outside a finite set; the Weil bounds on exterior powers and the resulting choice of the auxiliary integer N; the determinant character of the kernel computed by Raynaud's Theoreme 4.1.1, which is the one imported result this job could read in the original and whose file hash was re-verified here; the finiteness of invariant lattices; Satz 6, Shafarevich finiteness; and the two applications, the finiteness of curves of genus at least two with good reduction outside S and the Mordell conjecture through the Parshin construction.

The two interface statements: the commutant description at almost all primes, and Siegel's theorem obtained without Diophantine approximation. Both are recorded as the source states them; the audit records the layer as an interface over the previous two, none of whose results exist in either library.

gaps.title: The wild bound on the different exponent (Lemma 4) is planned by Tau Ceti but absent at the pin
gaps.detail: Lemma 4 (Hermite–Minkowski with ramification outside a finite S) closes with Mathlib's not_dvd_differentIdeal_iff, the discriminant tower formula NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_absNorm_differentIdeal_mul_natAbs_discr_pow and Hermite's NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd, except for one input: at a prime P over p ∈ S with ramification index e, v_P(different) ≤ e − 1 + v_P(e) (Serre, Local Fields III §6, remark after Proposition 13). Mathlib has only the lower bound (pow_sub_one_dvd_differentIdeal) and Tau Ceti only the tame equality (TauCeti.not_pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differentIdeal). The bound is planned by the Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic roadmap, layer 6.4 ('e ≤ v_P(𝔡) ≤ e − 1 + v_P(e) when it is wildly ramified'), existing work under section 15, but it is not at the pin, and the checker reads any prerequisite beginning 'tauceti:' as a baseline declaration, so the layer cannot be cited. Next action: cite the layer's declaration once it lands in Tau Ceti.

gaps.title: The proper Deligne–Mumford stack of stable curves M̄_g̃ over ℤ has no supplier

gaps.title: Zariski's main theorem is absent from the pinned libraries
gaps.detail: Lemma 1's proof ('Da A_1 normal ist, muß pr_1 ein Isomorphismus sein') needs: a proper quasi-finite morphism is finite, and a finite birational morphism onto a normal integral scheme is an isomorphism. Mathlib has the first only over a locally Artinian target (AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite) and neither Tau Ceti nor Mathlib has the second; no atlas stage names Zariski's main theorem (the Tau Ceti ModularCurves roadmap uses 'projective plus quasi-finite implies finite' without owning it). Next action: identify a foundational owner (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry or a scheme-foundations roadmap) or request it.

gaps.title: Tate's p-divisible groups paper (Driebergen 1966) is unread: the imports of §4 and of the erratum
gaps.detail: Faltings imports from [13] = Tate, p-divisible groups, Proceedings of a Conference on Local Fields (Driebergen 1966), Springer 1967, pp. 158-183: Proposition 2 (order of s*Ω¹ of the level-n piece, local differential count), Theorem 3 Corollary 2 (Hodge-Tate decomposition, Hodge-Tate determinant node), Theorem 2 (characters with C(ψ) ≅ C, determinant identity), and the erratum cites p. 182 for the discriminant argument of a). No public copy was found (web search, 24 September 2026; the Springer chapter is paywalled). The statements are routed as requests (R35.4 for Proposition 2, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 for Theorem 3, PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 for Theorem 2), but the discriminant argument of p. 182 has no supplier: its existence of n_0 in erratum a) is imported unread. Next source action: obtain Tate's paper and read Proposition 2, Theorems 2-4 and p. 182.

gaps.title: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX 7.4: orthogonality located and re-read; its proof through VIII 3.5 is unread
gaps.detail: Lemma 6 cites 'SGA VII, Exp. IX, §7' (p. 359) for ⟨T_l(T), T_l(H_i)⟩ = 0. Located and re-read on the page images of the public SLMath copy (SHA-256 reproduces the recorded hash): IX 7.3 (printed p. 407) fixes an arbitrary prime ℓ, including the residue characteristic, (7.3.1)-(7.3.2) identify the fixed part with T_ℓ(Â⁰) and the toric part with T_ℓ(T̂), (7.3.6) gives the ranks, and (7.4.2)-(7.4.3) (p. 409) say the biextension pairing on the fixed parts factors through the abelian parts. Not read: the proof of the factorization (SGA 7 I, VIII 3.5), and the identification of Faltings' polarization pairing with the biextension pairing (routine). The statement is requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3. Next source action: read SGA 7 I VIII 3.5 on the page images.

gaps.title: Class field theory over ℚ: routed through Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 except for the Raynaud determinant node
