The class field theory input of the determinant identity is now the new R28.2 character lemma, which rests on Kronecker-Weber in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-13-norm-theorems-and-class-fields (a request supplier, recorded on the node under upstreamPrerequisites because the checker reads 'tauceti:' prerequisites as baseline references). Still unrouted: the step 'Nach der Klassenkörpertheorie ist χ·ε^h eine Potenz des zyklotomischen Charakters χ_0' in the Raynaud determinant computation (p. 364), a mod-l character of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) unramified outside l; the same Layer 13 input proves it, and that node should cite Layer 13 (or a mod-l sibling of the character lemma) with the request.

gaps.title: The rational Torelli theorem has no owner in the atlas
gaps.detail: The proof of Korollar 1 to Satz 6 is 'Torelli'. What is used is the rational Torelli theorem: for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C of genus ≥ 2 over a perfect field k, the k-isomorphism class of C is determined by that of its principally polarized Jacobian (J(C), θ(C)). The statement and a proof sketch (original Torelli over k̄ plus Galois descent of the uniquely determined isomorphism) are in Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Theorem 4.2 and III §12 (public; statement read, proof of the geometric Torelli theorem not read). No atlas stage states it; the Tau Ceti Jacobian Challenge roadmap constructs Jacobians and their polarization but not Torelli. Only injectivity on isomorphism classes is needed, not the descent of a principally polarized abelian variety to a Jacobian over k.

gaps.title: Local Jordan–Zassenhaus: lattices over a maximal ℤ_l-order
gaps.detail: The finite-lattice node reduces the finiteness of isomorphism classes of π-stable lattices in a semisimple ℚ_l[π]-module to two facts about orders in a finite-dimensional semisimple ℚ_l-algebra B: (1) every ℤ_l-order in B is contained in a maximal order; (2) over a maximal order M' in B (ℚ_l complete), two M'-lattices spanning isomorphic B-modules are isomorphic. Neither is in the pinned libraries, and no source read for this review proves them (Faltings p. 363 asserts the finiteness from semisimplicity; Milne's review, p. 160, asserts it without proof). Standard reference, not read: I. Reiner, Maximal Orders. The R28.1 stage text requires this finite-lattice theorem to be proved in this roadmap or its general-algebra owner identified; no atlas stage owns it.

gaps.title: Raynaud's Théorème 4.1.1 has no supplier stage, and the exponent in it is not identified with #s*(Ω¹)
gaps.detail: Faltings' '[10], Théorème 4.11' is Raynaud's Théorème 4.1.1 (Bull. SMF 102 (1974), p. 272; read on the page image of the Numdam file, SHA-256 05cad2f5…edfe as recorded): for R strictly henselian of unequal characteristics (p. 271), 𝒢 finite flat commutative over R killed by p and e ≦ p − 1, Gal(K̄/K) acts on det(G) through the tame character τ_p^{v(𝔇̄(𝒢))}, where 𝔇̄(𝒢) is the absolute different (appendix, Définition 8, p. 279, read). Two inputs are missing: (1) a supplier for the theorem itself — FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1's stage text scopes Raynaud §§2–3 (Corollary 3.3.6, Theorems 3.4.1/3.4.3), not §4; (2) the identification v(𝔇̄(𝒢)) = length_R s*(Ω¹_{𝒢/R}) (the different of a finite flat group scheme over a discrete valuation ring equals the Fitting ideal of its co-Lie module), which Faltings uses tacitly to write the exponent as d with l^d = #s*(Ω¹_{G/R}); neither Faltings nor Raynaud states it. Checked cases: μ_p over ℤ_p^{ur} (different (p), co-Lie module ℤ_p/p, character χ_0) and ℤ/p (both trivial). Next action: extend R07.1 to Raynaud §4.1 or record the theorem as an import with its hypotheses, and source the different/Ω¹ identification (e.g. Tate, Finite flat group schemes, in Modular Forms and Fermat's Last Theorem).

gaps.title: Satz 7 and Bemerkung 1 belong to RP.4; the Parshin construction's implicit inputs
gaps.detail: HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.4 owns the Parshin covering reduction (Mordell) and Siegel finiteness for affine curves; neither is a target of R28.5 or R28.6. This review set realises to [] for the Satz 7 and Bemerkung 1 nodes, keeping them as records of Faltings' text; RP.4 consumes the curve corollary of R28.5. Faltings' proof of Satz 7 uses without statement: de Franchis' theorem (Milne, Abelian Varieties, IV Theorem 5.2, statement and proof read), genus(Y(x)) ≥ 2, and a finite extension of K_1 independent of x over which Y(x) and its map to X are defined (Lemma 4 applied to the fields of definition of the components of the 2-covering). Milne IV §5 (Theorems 5.1, 5.2, read) gives a complete version of the construction, different from Faltings' (2-division of the Jacobian and a square root of a function rather than the generalized Jacobian of (X_1, D)). Parshin [9] was not read. Orchestrator decision: merge the two nodes into RP.4 or keep them as source records.

gaps.title: No bridge from Weierstrass curves to Tau Ceti abelian varieties
gaps.detail: The R28.6 stage asks to export semisimplicity, the Hom comparison, isogeny detection and the finiteness of isogeny classes to the existing elliptic-curve type. Tau Ceti has Weierstrass curves with an isogeny Hom group (TauCeti.Isogeny.Hom, point- and function-field based) and, separately, abelian varieties over a field as group schemes (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety), but no functor from elliptic curves to one-dimensional abelian varieties. The export needs: for an elliptic curve E/K an abelian variety A_E of dimension 1 with (i) a group isomorphism Hom_K(E, E') ≅ Hom_K(A_E, A_E') compatible with composition and degree, (ii) a Galois-equivariant T_l(E) ≅ T_l(A_E), (iii) good reduction of E at v iff of A_E, (iv) the canonical principal polarization of A_E, with K-isomorphisms of E matching those of (A_E, λ). No atlas stage states this bridge; candidates are Tau Ceti EllipticCurves (which defers schemes to 'the future scheme-facing roadmap') and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 (Tate modules of elliptic curves and abelian varieties).

gaps.title: Zarhin's trick and the finiteness of direct factors have no node
gaps.detail: The unpolarized Shafarevich theorem (R28.5 stage target) follows from Satz 6 through (1) Zarhin's trick: (A × A^∨)^4 carries a principal polarization over the ground field (Milne, Abelian Varieties, I Theorem 13.12, read); (2) up to isomorphism an abelian variety has only finitely many direct factors (Milne I Theorem 15.3, read; the proof uses Borel–Harish-Chandra finiteness for arithmetic groups, not read); (3) the dual of an abelian variety with good reduction outside S has good reduction outside S. The R28.1 stage text assigns 'Zarhin's trick … with a proof of the resulting finiteness transfer' to R28.1, but no R28.1 node states it; the unpolarized node cites the stage FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.1 until one exists.

gaps.title: Bemerkung 2 (integral commutant for almost all l) has no proof in any source read
gaps.detail: Faltings deduces it from Satz 6 'mit Hilfe der Methode aus [16]' without proof. The rational version for all l follows from Satz 3/4 (Milne IV Corollary 2.7). The integral version needs, for almost all l, the mod-l analogue of Zarhin's lemma (every π-stable subspace of A[l] is the image of an element of End_K(A) ⊗ 𝔽_l, using the finiteness of the isogeny class) together with the double centralizer theorem over 𝔽_l and Nakayama. Zarhin's papers (Izv. 1974, 1975) and later expositions were not read.

requests.need: Semistable reduction of an abelian variety after a finite extension, Grothendieck's criterion that A acquires semistable reduction over K(A[m]) for m ≥ 3 prime to the residue characteristic, the monodromy criterion (semistable at v ∤ l iff inertia acts unipotently on T_l), and invariance of semistable reduction under isogeny.

For abelian varieties A, B over a field k and l ≠ char k: (1) Hom_k(A, B) is a free ℤ-module of finite rank ≤ 4·dim A·dim B, and Hom_k(A, B) ⊗ ℤ_l → Hom(T_l A, T_l B) is injective with torsion-free cokernel; (2) End_k(A) ⊗ ℚ is a semisimple ℚ-algebra (Poincaré complete reducibility); (3) End_k(A^n) = M_n(End_k(A)) and End_k(A × B) is the 2 × 2 block ring, compatibly with T_l; (4) the automorphism group of a polarized abelian variety is finite; (5) a polarization λ of degree d descends along the quotient by a subgroup of ker λ that is maximal isotropic for e^λ to a polarization of degree d/#H², in particular a principal one when #H = √d; (6) the dual of an abelian scheme is an abelian scheme; and, as already requested, (7) the Galois-equivariant comparison T_l(Res_{K/ℚ} A) ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_ℚ} T_l(A).
The Weil bound for abelian varieties: the eigenvalues of Frobenius on the Tate module of an abelian variety over 𝔽_q have absolute value q^{1/2}, and its consequence for exterior powers.

For an abelian variety A over a number field K and a prime l: (1) T_l(A) with its continuous G_K-action, T_l(A × B) = T_l(A) ⊕ T_l(B); (2) an isogeny φ : A → B induces an injective T_l(φ) whose cokernel has order the l-part of deg φ; (3) the Weil pairing e^λ : T_l(A) × T_l(A) → ℤ_l(1) of a polarization λ, alternating, Galois-equivariant, nondegenerate when λ is principal, and orthogonal-sum for products; (4) at a place v ∤ l of good reduction, the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on T_l(A) has integer coefficients independent of l (the local Euler factor), and the local factor at a bad place defined through the inertia invariants; (5) the same for elliptic curves, compatibly with the Tate module of Tau Ceti's Weierstrass curves.

The arithmetic degree of a metrized line bundle on Spec(O_K) in Faltings' normalisation: for a projective rank-one O_K-module P with norms ‖·‖_v on P ⊗ K_v at the infinite places, deg(P) = log #(P/O_K·p) − Σ_v mult(v)·log ‖p‖_v for any p ≠ 0 (mult as Mathlib's InfinitePlace.mult), independent of p; deg(P ⊗ O_{K'}) = [K':K]·deg(P) for finite K'/K; and the comparison with Mathlib's heights: for x ∈ ℙ^n(K) with ρ_x: Spec(O_K) → ℙ^n_ℤ and a continuous hermitian metric on O(1) over ℙ^n(ℂ), |deg ρ_x^*O(1) − [K:ℚ]·Projectivization.logHeight x| ≤ [K:ℚ]·C with C depending only on the metric.

For a semiabelian scheme p: A → S of relative dimension g with zero section s (ShimuraCompactifications:C4): the Hodge line ω_{A/S} = s^*(Ω^g_{A/S}), its compatibility with every base change, ω_{A/S} ≅ p_*(Ω^g_{A/S}) when p is proper; and for a complex abelian variety the hermitian product ⟨α, β⟩ = 2^{−g} i^{g²} ∫_{A(ℂ)} α ∧ β̄ on Γ(A, Ω^g), positive definite (the factor i^{g²} = i^g (−1)^{g(g−1)/2} is needed: Faltings' printed (i/2)^g is negative for g ≡ 2, 3 mod 4), invariant under complex conjugation, with its relative version over a complex base where A is proper; and ‖φ^*α‖² = deg(φ)·‖α‖² for an isogeny φ (used in Section 4).

For K a number field and p: A → Spec(O_K) semiabelian with proper generic fibre: the height h(A) = deg(ω_{A/O_K}, Hodge metric)/[K:ℚ] (R35.1 degree, R35.2 metric), its invariance under base change to O_{K'} for finite K'/K, and its dependence only on A_K (the semiabelian model being unique by Faltings' Lemma 1, FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.1).

Semi-abelian schemes over an arbitrary base scheme (and over Deligne–Mumford stacks): smooth separated commutative group schemes whose fibres are connected extensions of abelian varieties by tori, with relative dimension, base change and restriction to opens; the object of Faltings' §2 Definition (p. 350). Also the semiabelian extension of the universal family over the toroidal compactification used with C2.

Over ℂ, for g ≥ 1: a smooth proper toroidal compactification N of a neat-level cover of A_g(ℂ), with normal-crossings boundary, and a proper dominant morphism φ: N → Ā_g(ℂ) to the Baily–Borel compactification, over which the universal abelian scheme extends to a semi-abelian scheme (C4) whose Hodge line satisfies ω^{⊗r} ≅ φ^*(M), M = O(1) of the Baily–Borel embedding (Namikawa [8] §9; the identity ω^{⊗r} ≅ φ^*(M) is Faltings [6] §2). This is fact 2 b), pp. 351–352.

For the Siegel datum of genus g: an r > 0 such that ω^{⊗r} of the universal principally polarized abelian scheme descends to a very ample line bundle on the coarse space A_g ⊗ ℚ, giving the projective minimal compactification Ā_g/ℚ ⊆ ℙ^N_ℚ with M = O(1) extending ω^{⊗r} (Baily–Borel [3]; fact 2 a), p. 351).

(i) The algebraic stack 𝔄_g over Spec(ℤ) of principally polarized abelian schemes of relative dimension g, its universal abelian scheme and Hodge line, and its coarse space A_g with A_g(K̄) = K̄-isomorphism classes; the moduli point x_A ∈ A_g(K) of a principally polarized A/K. (ii) The descent comparison: for a finite Galois K'/K, the K-forms of a polarized abelian variety (A, λ)/K split by K' are in bijection with H^1(Gal(K'/K), Aut_{K'}(A, λ)).
Serre's rigidity: for n ≥ 3 and a polarized abelian variety (A, λ) over a field of characteristic prime to n, an automorphism of (A, λ) acting trivially on A[n] is the identity.

Deligne–Mumford stacks over Spec(ℤ): proper morphisms and their valuative criterion (a K-point of the target of a proper surjective morphism lifts, after a finite extension K'/K, to an O_{K'}-point of the source), closures of graphs of rational maps, and the finite surjective scheme covers V_i → U_i of an open cover of the coarse space carrying the universal object (Faltings p. 351).
Normalisation and schematic closure for Deligne–Mumford stacks (J replaced by the normalisation of the closure of a graph in Lemma 2), and coarse spaces with their base change.

Over a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K: a homomorphism between the generic fibres of two semiabelian schemes with abelian generic fibres extends uniquely to a homomorphism of group schemes (a semiabelian scheme is the identity component of the Néron model of its generic fibre, Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud 7.4 Proposition 3, plus the Néron mapping property).

For a stable curve q: C → S of genus g over a scheme or Deligne–Mumford stack S: Pic^τ(C/S) = Pic^0(C/S) is a semiabelian scheme of relative dimension g (Faltings' Beispiel, p. 350), its Lie algebra is R^1 q_*O_C, and its Hodge line is Λ^g q_*(ω_{C/S}) with ω_{C/S} the relative dualising sheaf (Bemerkung c)).

For abelian varieties over a number field K: (i) Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich: good reduction at v ∤ n implies A[n] unramified at v; (ii) good reduction is preserved under isogeny; (iii) for A with semistable reduction at v, good reduction at v is equivalent to potentially good reduction at v, so for abelian varieties with semistable reduction everywhere the bad places depend only on the K̄-isomorphism class; (iv) Grothendieck's criterion: A has semistable reduction over K(A[m]) at the places not dividing m, for m ≥ 3.

For an abelian variety B/K with a polarization μ whose kernel is a constant group scheme, and H ⊆ ker μ maximal isotropic for the Weil pairing e^μ: the quotient B/H by the finite subgroup H exists, #H² = deg μ, and μ descends to a unique principal polarization μ' on B/H with π^*μ' = μ (Mumford, Abelian Varieties §23).

The analytification X(ℂ) of a finite-type ℂ-scheme and of a line bundle (or vector bundle) M on it as a holomorphic bundle with local trivialisations, compatible with pullback along morphisms, so that continuous hermitian metrics on M|(X(ℂ) − Y(ℂ)), their tensor powers, determinants and pullbacks can be defined.

Two things. (1) Faltings' Lemma 5 in the normalisation of this packet: for semiabelian A_1, A_2 over O_K with proper generic fibres and an isogeny φ: A_1 → A_2 (given over K and extended over O_K), φ is flat, G = Ker φ is a quasi-finite flat commutative group scheme killed by Grad(φ), φ*: ω_{A_2} → ω_{A_1} is injective with cokernel s*(Ω¹_{A_1/A_2}) = s*(Ω¹_{G/O_K}), φ* multiplies the Hodge norm (i/2)^g∫α∧ᾱ at every infinite place by Grad(φ) (the norm by Grad(φ)^{1/2}), hence h(A_2) = h(A_1) + ½ log Grad(φ) − [K:ℚ]^{-1} log #s*(Ω¹_{G/O_K}) for the height h = Grad(ω)/[K:ℚ] with e_v = 1, 2 at real and complex places. (2) The local term for primes dividing the degree (Tate, p-divisible groups, Proposition 2): for an l-divisible group Γ of dimension d over the valuation ring R_i of K_i/ℚ_l of degree m_i, s*(Ω¹_{Γ[l^n]/R_i}) ≅ (R_i/l^n)^d, so its order is l^{n m_i d}.

For abelian varieties over a field of characteristic 0 (and their semiabelian models where stated): (1) the degree of an isogeny φ as the order of its finite kernel, a quasi-inverse ψ with ψ∘φ = [deg φ], so deg φ kills ker φ; (2) the alternating, Galois-equivariant, nondegenerate pairing T_l(A) × T_l(A) → ℤ_l(1) of a polarization, and the pairing e^λ on ker λ (alternating, nondegenerate, order of ker λ a square); (3) descent of polarizations: for an isogeny π: A → B with ker π ⊆ ker λ isotropic for e^λ there is a unique polarization μ of B with λ = π^∨∘μ∘π, and deg λ = deg μ·(deg π)² (Milne, Abelian Varieties, Prop. 13.8 and Rem. 13.9; Mumford §23); (4) the product polarization on A × B, its degree and the orthogonal-sum pairing on T_l(A × B).

Over the valuation ring R_i of a finite extension K_i/ℚ_l: l-divisible groups with their generic fibres, Tate modules, height and dimension of the connected part; the schematic closure of a finite subgroup of the generic fibre of a finite flat (or formal) group is finite flat; the finite part of a quasi-finite separated flat commutative group scheme over the henselian R_i (open and closed, finite over R_i, containing the unit section) and its generic fibre as the points that extend.

For a semiabelian scheme over a complete discrete valuation ring R_i with special fibre an extension of an abelian variety by a torus T_s: the lift T of T_s over R_i, its character group X*(T) with the unramified Galois action through a finite quotient, and the identification Hom(T_l(T), ℤ_l(1)) ≅ X*(T) ⊗ ℤ_l; the ranks t = dim T_s and 2 dim B_s + t of the toric and fixed parts.

Tate's Theorem 2 and its converse for a finite extension F/ℚ_l with C the completion of F̄ and a continuous character ψ: Gal(F̄/F) → ℤ_l^×: C(ψ) ≅ C as semilinear modules if and only if ψ has finite image on inertia (equivalently H^0(Gal(F̄/F), C(ψ)) = 0 when ψ(I) is infinite); and a continuous ℚ_l-representation with finite image becomes trivial after ⊗C.

Tate's Hodge-Tate decomposition (Tate, p-divisible groups, Theorem 3 and Corollary 2): for an l-divisible group Γ of height h and dimension d over the valuation ring of a finite extension F/ℚ_l, V_l(Γ) ⊗_{ℚ_l} C ≅ C^{h−d} ⊕ C(1)^d as semilinear Gal(F̄/F)-modules.
Kronecker-Weber ('kroneckerWeber' in the layer text): every finite abelian extension of ℚ lies in a cyclotomic field, so that Gal(ℚ^ab/ℚ) ≅ lim_n (ℤ/n)^× via the cyclotomic characters.

Induction and restriction of continuous representations of profinite groups on finite free ℤ_l-modules: the Mackey decomposition of Res_D Ind_H^G over the double cosets D\G/H, exterior powers, and the determinant of an induced representation det Ind_H^G U = sgn_{G/H}^{rank U}·(det U ∘ Ver_{G→H}).

Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich for abelian varieties over number fields: A has good reduction at v ∤ l iff G_K acts on T_l(A) unramified at v; hence isogenous abelian varieties have the same places of good reduction, and the Galois representation of an abelian variety with good reduction outside S is unramified outside S and the places above l.
For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields, every conjugacy class of Gal(L/K) is the Frobenius class of infinitely many primes of K (so of primes avoiding any given finite set).
Ramification in ℚ(ζ_n): only primes dividing n ramify, and for n = l^a·n' with l ∤ n' the inertia groups at the primes dividing n' generate Gal(ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ(ζ_{l^a})) ≅ (ℤ/n')^*.
The dual isogeny: for a nonzero f ∈ Hom_K(E, E') of Weierstrass curves there is a nonzero f̂ ∈ Hom_K(E', E) with f̂ ∘ f = [deg f].
The Tate module T_l(E) of a Weierstrass curve E over a field of characteristic 0 with its continuous Galois action, free of rank 2 over ℤ_l, and the action of Tau Ceti's Hom_K(E, E') on Tate modules.

Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich for elliptic curves over a number field: E has good reduction at v iff T_l(E) is unramified at v for l ≠ char k(v); hence K-isogenous curves have the same places of good reduction.

The Jacobian J(X) of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over a field, and for a smooth proper curve over a discrete valuation ring the relative Jacobian as an abelian scheme, so that good reduction of X gives good reduction of J(X).
The canonical principal polarization of the Jacobian (the theta divisor), compatible with isomorphisms of curves.

restructure.title: The Chebotarev and class field theory suppliers of this roadmap need re-pointing
restructure.detail: The reviewed integrated decomposition added five supplier links from FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4, which was retired on the day of that review. This packet does not use them. Two of the five inputs are Chebotarev, and the pinned Tau Ceti library already has a Chebotarev development, so they are baseline citations here. The remaining three are class field theory over the rationals, for which the retirement record names a covering Tau Ceti roadmap whose layer identifiers cannot appear as prerequisites. The proposal is that the atlas give this roadmap an explicit supplier stage for class field theory, or that the covering roadmap's layers be given identifiers of the ordinary stage form so that they can be named.

restructure.title: R28.5 carries two different jobs and should be divided
restructure.detail: R28.5 contains both the finiteness theorems themselves, Satz 5 and Satz 6 with their inputs, and the two applications that follow from them, the finiteness of curves of genus at least two with good reduction outside S and the Mordell conjecture through the Parshin construction. The two halves have different acceptance tests: the first is measured against the source's own proof, the second against the statement of Torelli's theorem and the Parshin construction, both of which this roadmap imports rather than proves, and the second of which the atlas already assigns to HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.4. Dividing the layer would make the boundary between what this roadmap proves and what it consumes visible in the atlas, and would stop the curve corollary and Mordell appearing to be part of the same body of work as the finiteness theorems.

review.notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-2aeb03 (the blueprint is by cc-7b31c4). Faltings 1983 was re-read in full on the page images of the public GDZ scan, the erratum on the free Springer PDF, and Raynaud 1974 and SGA 7 I IX on their public copies; Milne's public Abelian Varieties notes were added for the Zarhin and Tate-conjecture arguments Faltings cites. Every one of the 32 original nodes was corrected (locators, literal German excerpts, statements, prerequisites, splits); 24 nodes were added for hidden steps, split results and unrealised stage targets; one duplicate proposal was merged. The packet no longer defines objects other roadmaps own (semiabelian schemes: ShimuraCompactifications C4; the Hodge line, arithmetic degree and height: ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.1-R35.3); those nodes became a lemma and a comparison with requests. Statements that the erratum refutes (the height formula and the local count for A itself) are stated under the explicit hypothesis R28.3 establishes. Baseline: every citation read at the pins; 5 removed (a near miss for Hermite–Minkowski replaced by NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd, and four unused or wrong), 33 added. 22 source issues recorded and confirmed (E8 is Satz 2 as printed, corrected by the erratum). The suggested Lean file stated every theorem and structure field as True; it is rewritten with honest statements and elaborates against the pins. Status needs_changes only because the roadmap document research/blueprint/readmes/FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.md, which this review may not edit, still describes the uncorrected packet and must be regenerated from it before promotion.
